SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/sapience/ (never .claude/**, a disposable deploy artifact -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Redeploy afterwards via deploy-headless.sh.

Create a sapience extension modeled on agent-system/extensions/memory/. Sapience (app.spnc.ai) is the hosted knowledge vault configured by modules/home/services/sapience.nix; see ~/.dotfiles/docs/sapience.md for the full machine configuration. Scope and sequencing below were settled by direct reading of ~/.sapience/{mcp.py,sf1.py,upload.py}, ~/.dotfiles/config/claude/settings.json, ~/.claude.json, and agent-system/extensions/memory/.

ALREADY AMBIENT -- DO NOT REBUILD: the MCP server registration in ~/.claude.json (mcpServers.sapience, written by the nix module's activation), and three hooks already present in ~/.dotfiles/config/claude/settings.json: SessionStart -> `mcp.py --briefing-text`, SessionEnd -> `mcp.py --receipt`, Stop -> `mcp.py --effect-line`. An extension that re-registers any of these is dead weight. Note also that those hook/permission keys are ENFORCED by home.activation.claudeSettings, which resets them from the dotfiles repo on every home-manager switch -- so the extension must not attempt to write them.

GAP 1 (the blocker; sequence first -- gaps 2 and 3 are unreachable until it is closed). The seven mcp__sapience__* entries in the dotfiles permissions.allow list are all READ-only: sapience_search, sapience_briefing, sapience_context, sapience_ask, sapience_outstanding, sapience_papers, plus a literal "mcp__sapience__sapience" entry that does not name any real tool and should be checked for whether it silently matches nothing. The WRITE tools -- sapience_remember, sapience_wrapup, sapience_handoff, sapience_adddoc -- are absent, so an autonomous dispatch that tries to save a finding hits a permission prompt and fails non-interactively. Close this with permissions.allow grants in the extension's own settings-fragment.json, which merges into the project-scoped, deploy-regenerated .claude/settings.local.json -- a different file from the ~/.claude/settings.json the activation enforces, so there is no conflict with the enforced-key mechanism.

CONSTRAINT FROM AN OPEN SIBLING (task 29, generate_mcp_json_from_extension_manifests): that task records that `mcpServers` keys inside settings-fragment.json register NOTHING, because settings files are not a server-registration surface. That finding concerns server registration and does NOT invalidate this approach -- permissions.allow is a genuine settings.json key and a distinct concern from mcpServers. The extension must therefore carry permission grants ONLY and must not declare an mcpServers block. Consult agent-system/extensions/core/context/patterns/mcp-server-ownership.md (the artifact produced by the completed task 241, reconcile_mcp_registration_surfaces) for the canonical ownership split between registration and permission surfaces before writing settings-fragment.json.

GAP 2. source_skip() in ~/.sapience/upload.py classifies each transcript as `subagent` or `harness-started` from its opening turns and those are NEVER read; the run logs them as "thread mechanics; never read" and the message states outright that SAPIENCE_INCLUDE_HEADLESS=1 does not override it. Measured on this machine: 1013 of 1295 transcripts on disk are removed by this filter, against 203 eligible. Because most work in this repo runs through orchestrated dispatch, agent work therefore CANNOT reach the vault by extraction at all -- the only path in is an explicit tool call during the run. Close it with a postflight wrapup instruction: 3-8 distilled notes per completed task, written from the summary artifact at the [IMPLEMENTING] -> [COMPLETED] transition. Do NOT instead instruct every agent to fire sapience_remember mid-run. That scoping is deliberate and load-bearing: sapience_remember via MCP writes straight to the hosted vault rather than staging a finding, so it bypasses the `sapience review` gate that config.json auto_approve=false exists to preserve; a per-agent proactive-save instruction would flood the vault with unreviewed content across an /orchestrate batch.

GAP 3 (weakest case; sequence last). Subagents receive no briefing, because SessionStart fires for the root session only, so every /orchestrate research/plan/implement dispatch begins with no vault orientation. Use the top-level manifest.json "hooks" object with a context_injection entry -- the mechanism already exercised by the nix and nvim extensions. See agent-system/extensions/nvim/scripts/nvim-context.sh for the stable 5-positional-arg calling contract (task_number, task_type, task_dir, session_id, operation) invoked by skill_context_injection() in skill-base.sh. Keep the hook CHEAP: statusline-grade, or cached once per session. mcp.py exposes NO --search and NO --ask CLI mode (the available modes are --briefing-text, --statusline, --stats, --status, --receipt, --effect-line, --adddoc, --adddir, --refresh-cache), so any shell-side query must go through `sf1 "question"` one-shot or a direct curl to /v1/ask -- i.e. a network round-trip on every dispatch.

EXPLICIT ANTI-GOAL -- DO NOT ADD A SECOND PER-DISPATCH RETRIEVAL INJECTION. memory-retrieve.sh is local, keyword-scored against .memory/memory-index.json, zero-network, capped at a 2000-token budget and 5 entries. A sapience equivalent would add a network round-trip to every agent in a batch. Split the two systems by altitude instead: sapience for session-level orientation and cross-project recall, the memory extension for per-dispatch injection. The two must not compete for the same context budget.

DELIVERABLE file set, modeled on agent-system/extensions/memory/: manifest.json; EXTENSION.md (merged into .claude/CLAUDE.md under section_id extension_sapience); index-entries.json; settings-fragment.json (the permission grants -- the actual payload of gap 1); scripts/sapience-context.sh (the gap 3 hook); context/project/sapience/ with a README.md plus domain notes covering the vault model, the review-gate boundary (what staging means and what bypasses it), and the transcript-filter ceiling that motivates gap 2.

EXPLICIT NON-GOALS. (a) No task_type and no routing_agents in the manifest: sapience is not a domain one implements in, so a research/plan/implement triple would route to agents with nothing to research. (b) No /sapience slash command wrapping the CLI -- review, sync, coverage, pending and stats are terminal verbs already covered by the three GNOME desktop launchers the nix module installs. (c) No re-registration of the MCP server or of the three existing hooks. (d) No mcpServers block in settings-fragment.json (see the task 29 constraint above).

active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/ (never .claude/**, a disposable deploy artifact -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Redeploy afterwards via deploy-headless.sh using the bounded-wait idiom (timeout 540, Bash tool timeout raised to 600000), never a hand-patch of a deployed file. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (both are permitted in this description).

GOAL. Collapse the two divergent implementations of /todo into one authoritative implementation, and fix an `archived_projects`-blind detection bug once in the survivor rather than twice in the copies. NET DELETION.

=== THIS IS A REVIVAL, AND 328 CANNOT ABSORB IT ===
This work is the first phase of the abandoned record `todo_consolidate_and_optimize`, which was abandoned into `systematic_script_and_test_corpus_efficiency` (planned). That record cannot deliver it. Its acceptance criterion is explicitly behavior-preserving -- "complete on a measured net reduction in corpus size, with every gate's finding set and every suite's assertion set provably unchanged" (verified verbatim in its description, 2026-11-02). Consolidating /todo requires DECIDING WHICH IMPLEMENTATION IS AUTHORITATIVE, which changes behavior wherever the two diverge, so it fails that criterion by construction. Corroborating measurement, 2026-11-02: that record's live plan `plans/03_markdown-corpus-consolidation.md` mentions `skill-todo` ZERO times and `CHANGE_LOG` ZERO times -- the work is not in its plan and was not silently inherited. Revive it here; do not re-abandon it into that record.

=== THE DUPLICATION (all figures re-measured 2026-11-02; re-measure again before quoting) ===
`skills/skill-todo/SKILL.md` hand-implements the same archival stages that `commands/todo.md` implements, and `commands/todo.md` NEVER DISPATCHES IT.
  - `commands/todo.md`: 886 lines. The string `skill-todo` appears ZERO times in it. Its allowed-tools line (line 3) is `Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash(git:*), Bash(mv:*), Bash(mkdir:*), Bash(ls:*), Bash(find:*), Bash(jq:*), TaskCreate, TaskUpdate, AskUserQuestion` -- NO Skill entry, so it could not dispatch the skill even if it named it.
  - `skills/skill-todo/SKILL.md`: 1120 lines (the abandoned record measured ~1,170; the live figure is 1120). Combined /todo footprint 2006 lines, of which the never-dispatched skill is roughly 56%.
  - Every out-of-directory reference to `skill-todo` is documentation, manifest registration, a merge source, a lint registry or a test -- none is a dispatch. Measured: 21 files outside `skills/skill-todo/` mention it, concentrated in `scripts/tests/test-todo-move-pair-staging.sh` (18 mentions, a test), plus `manifest.json`, `merge-sources/claudemd.md`, `context/reference/skill-agent-mapping.md`, `context/architecture/system-overview.md`, `scripts/lint/lint-postflight-boundary.sh`, `scripts/lint/lint-state-writer-boundary.sh`, `scripts/validate-state.sh`, `scripts/skill-base.sh`, `scripts/memory-harvest.sh` and others. Re-enumerate before acting: that set determines the blast radius of either direction below.

=== FRAME AS CONSOLIDATION, NOT DELETION ===
`skill-todo` is manifest-registered and deployed, so it appears in the harness's own Skill listing and IS invocable as `Skill(skill-todo)` even though `/todo` never calls it. DELETING THE FILE ALONE BREAKS THAT PATH. Pick ONE source of truth, then either:
  (a) make the other a thin delegator to the survivor, or
  (b) remove it TOGETHER WITH its `manifest.json` registration, its `index-entries.json` entry if present, and every registry/lint reference that would otherwise dangle, in the same change.
Then reconcile the documentation. Do not leave a registered-but-absent skill or an unregistered-but-present one; `validate-index.sh` and the agent/skill contract lints are the mechanical check on that.

=== ALSO CORRECT context/architecture/system-overview.md ===
Line 417 reads `| /todo | Direct | skill-todo | (no agent) | B |`, which places `skill-todo` in /todo's execution path. It is not in that path. The abandoned record identified this misleading row as the reason the duplication survived unnoticed -- a reader checking how /todo works is told the skill is involved. Re-verify the line number and the row's current text before editing it, and correct it to whatever the consolidation makes true.

=== WHAT THE DIVERGENCE HAS ALREADY COST (measured live, 2026-11-02 -- concrete, not hypothetical) ===
`skill-todo/SKILL.md` advertises automated CHANGE_LOG maintenance in its own frontmatter description ("Archive completed, abandoned, and expanded tasks with CHANGE_LOG.md updates and memory harvest suggestions") and in its `<role>` line, and carries CHANGE_LOG stages. `commands/todo.md` has NO CHANGE_LOG step at all -- the string `CHANGE_LOG` appears ZERO times in its 886 lines. Because the skill is never dispatched, those stages never run.

Consequence in a consumer repository, measured: `specs/CHANGE_LOG.md`'s newest entry is dated 2026-10-04, while FOUR archival runs have landed since -- 2026-10-09 (17 tasks), 2026-10-13 (19), 2026-10-15 (18) and 2026-11-02 (19), each a `todo: archive N completed tasks` commit. That is 73 archived tasks absent from a log whose own entries are titled "Archive N completed tasks". Nobody noticed for a month.

DO NOT FIX CHANGE_LOG HERE. The companion record `cross_task_traceability_and_changelog_verdict` owns the question of whether CHANGE_LOG should exist at all, and fixing it here would prejudge that. Cite this only as evidence of what two divergence surfaces cost.

=== FOLD IN: ORPHAN AND MISPLACED-DIRECTORY DETECTION IGNORES archived_projects (correctness bug) ===
Both implementations' orphan and misplaced-directory scans query ONLY `.completed_projects[]` in `specs/archive/state.json`. Abandoned tasks route to the SIBLING `.archived_projects[]` array, so every directory belonging to an abandoned-then-archived task reads as UNTRACKED -- an orphan that is not one. The archive write itself is correct (it populates both arrays); only the read-back is blind.

RE-COUNTED 2026-11-02: SIX occurrences of the defective lookup, exactly as the abandoned record measured. `commands/todo.md` lines 71, 88 and 127 (orphans-in-specs, orphans-in-archive, and the misplaced-directory scan at section 2.6); `skills/skill-todo/SKILL.md` lines 246, 263 and 294 (the same three scans). Re-derive these line numbers before editing -- they shift with any other change to either file.

THIS IS WHY THE BUG BELONGS IN THIS RECORD RATHER THAN ITS OWN. Fixing it before consolidating means fixing it twice and leaving the two copies free to diverge again on the fix. Fix it ONCE, in the survivor.

Confirmed still live: a /todo run in a consumer repository on 2026-11-02 used the defective query. It happened to find zero orphans, so nothing was mis-archived, but the scan was not trustworthy and a clean result from it proves nothing.

=== SECOND DUPLICATION SURFACE, NEWLY MEASURED: THE VAULT OPERATION ===
The vault operation -- the single riskiest state transform in the system, which renumbers active tasks by subtracting 1000 and resets `next_project_number` -- is ALSO implemented twice. `commands/todo.md` section 5.7 ("Vault Operation (when next_project_number > 1000)", with the renumber at step 5.7.7) and `skills/skill-todo/SKILL.md` stage 10 both carry it, including both AskUserQuestion confirmation prompts and both dependency-array rewrites. `context/reference/state-management-schema.md`'s "Renumber survival" discussion names `commands/todo.md`'s step as THE live renumbering path, and separately quarantines `scripts/deprecated/vault-operation.sh` as an older copy that is NOT the live path. A third live copy inside the never-dispatched skill is the same hazard that quarantine exists to prevent. Treat the vault operation as a first-class part of the consolidation, not an incidental block: whichever implementation survives must be the one the schema document names, or that document must be corrected in the same change.

=== COLLISION FIELD IS CLEAR (verified 2026-11-02) ===
The two records the abandoned task named as competing editors of `commands/todo.md` -- a scoped-commit pathspec change and the `commands/task.md` slimming record -- are both terminal and archived. Those overlap notes are STALE; do not carry them forward as live.
Current measurement: NO non-terminal record's file_scope names `commands/todo.md` or `skill-todo`. One record does name `skills/skill-todo/SKILL.md` in its file_scope -- `archival_silently_untracks_evidence_gate_targets` -- but its status is `completed`, awaiting archival only. Re-run the check at dispatch time; it is one jq query over `active_projects[].file_scope`.

=== WHY THIS SHAPE IS RIGHT ===
`systematic_script_and_test_corpus_efficiency` measured the backlog's additive-to-reductive ratio: roughly SIXTEEN non-terminal records add machinery (a lint, gate, guard, warning, chokepoint or enforcement) against roughly THREE that reduce it, and concluded that working the backlog to completion makes the system larger. This record is net deletion AND a correctness fix at once, so it runs WITH that doctrine rather than against it. Declare a net-line figure and report it; a consolidation that does not reduce total lines has probably become a rewrite and should be re-scoped.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===
- ONE authoritative /todo implementation. The other is a thin delegator to it, or is removed together with its manifest registration and every registry/lint reference that would otherwise dangle.
- `Skill(skill-todo)` either still resolves (delegator kept) or is deliberately and completely deregistered -- never registered-but-absent.
- `context/architecture/system-overview.md`'s /todo routing row states what is actually true after the change.
- The `archived_projects` detection bug is fixed ONCE, in the surviving copy, across all three scans (orphans-in-specs, orphans-in-archive, misplaced directories). A fixture or test demonstrates that an abandoned-then-archived task directory is no longer reported as an orphan.
- The vault operation exists in exactly one live place, and `context/reference/state-management-schema.md`'s "Renumber survival" section names that place correctly.
- `validate-index.sh`, `validate-state.sh`, `lint-agent-contracts.sh`, `lint-postflight-boundary.sh` and `lint-state-writer-boundary.sh` are all green; `scripts/tests/test-todo-move-pair-staging.sh` and `test-validate-state.sh` still pass or are updated with their assertions' intent preserved.
- A REPORTED NET-LINE FIGURE (lines before, lines after, delta).
- Redeployed via deploy-headless.sh to a clean verify-deploy.sh.

active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/ (never .claude/**, a disposable deploy artifact -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Redeploy afterwards via deploy-headless.sh using the bounded-wait idiom (timeout 540, Bash tool timeout raised to 600000), never a hand-patch of a deployed file. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (both are permitted in this description).

CLASSIFICATION: RESEARCH-AND-DESIGN, VERDICT-FIRST. NO IMPLEMENTATION BEFORE THE DESIGN IS RECORDED AND ACCEPTED. The deliverable is a recorded design with a verdict, not a landed mechanism. A pull toward "just build the obvious thing" is the main way this record goes wrong.

GOAL, in the terms it was asked for: improve the dependencies and references between open, closed and archived records so that CHANGES ARE EASY TO TRACE, referencing the DECISIONS MADE in each record -- and retire `specs/CHANGE_LOG.md` only IF APPROPRIATE, as an OUTCOME of that design rather than a premise. Do not pre-decide retirement. Do not pre-decide a mechanism.

=== THE PROBLEM ===
Work is traceable today only by reading scattered artifacts by hand. There is no path from "this changed" to "which record changed it and on what grounds", and no path from a recorded decision to the places it governs.

RAW MATERIAL THAT ALREADY EXISTS. The research must INVENTORY each of these against the live tree rather than assume its shape or its contents:
  - `dependencies[]` on each `active_projects[]` entry -- ordering edges, consumed by the Kahn-algorithm wave computation.
  - `parent_task` -- a LINEAGE pointer, explicitly NOT a dependency edge. `context/reference/state-management-schema.md`'s "Parent Task Field" section states that a child's dispatch eligibility never consults its parent and that `parent_task` is absent from the wave computation entirely; lineage and ordering "may point in opposite directions for the same pair without contradiction". This is the closest thing the system already has to a traceability edge, and it is deliberately inert.
  - `artifacts[]` on each entry.
  - Per-record `issues.jsonl` and `metrics.jsonl`, `handoffs/`, `records/`, `reports/`, `plans/`, `summaries/`, and `.return-meta.json`. All seven of these were confirmed present in live record directories on 2026-11-02; `prototype/` appears in at least one. Do not assume every record has every one.
  - `specs/events.jsonl` -- a single append-only repository-wide log (2.2 MB in one consumer repository at measurement).
  - `specs/archive/state.json` and its TWO sibling arrays, `completed_projects[]` and `archived_projects[]`.
  - Git history, including the `task {N}: {action}` commit convention.
  - `specs/CHANGE_LOG.md` itself.

=== THE CENTRAL DESIGN TENSION: TASK NUMBERS ARE NOT DURABLE ===
Any proposal must confront this head-on rather than route around it.

A vault operation renumbers active records by SUBTRACTING 1000 and resets `next_project_number`. `rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md` exists precisely because of this: it states that "task numbers are renumbered during vault operations" and are meaningless to a future reader, which is why deliverables must cite durable anchors instead. `context/reference/state-management-schema.md`'s "Renumber survival" section works through which fields the transform rewrites and which it strands -- and documents an actual casualty, a top-level `.artifacts[0].path` pointing at a directory name that is orphaned residue from a recycled number and exists in neither the working tree nor git history. That is this record's problem in miniature, already observed.

Worse, there are AT LEAST TWO INDEPENDENT COUNTERS -- a consumer repository's and this source store's -- and records in this task space already warn that the other repository renumbers on vault operations and that a number must be RE-RESOLVED BY DESCRIPTION rather than trusted. So any traceability scheme keyed on record numbers is broken by construction, in two ways at once: numbers are reused over time, and the same number denotes different work in different repositories.

SHARPEST INSTANCE, WHICH THE RESEARCH MUST ADDRESS EXPLICITLY. The git commit convention is `task {N}: {action}` (`rules/git-workflow.md`, with the standard action table). This bakes a MUTABLE number into IMMUTABLE history. After a vault operation, historical commit messages point at numbers that now denote different records, and nothing in history records which epoch a message belongs to. Say what, if anything, to do about it -- INCLUDING the legitimate answer that it is accepted and worked around rather than fixed. Rewriting history is not an option; changing the convention going forward has a cost; adding an epoch marker is a third option. Pick one and give the grounds.

=== PRECEDENT ALREADY IN THE SYSTEM -- BUILD ON IT, DO NOT REINVENT ===
  - MINTED STABLE IDS ALREADY EXIST AND ARE ALREADY CITED. `issues.jsonl` entries carry `entry_id` of the form `iss_{timestamp_ms}_{random6}` -- verified live, e.g. an entry beginning `iss_1791533278944_` with a six-character suffix. `context/formats/issue-log.md` specifies the form and states that it mirrors `events.jsonl`'s `event_id` and `errors.json`'s `err_{timestamp}` conventions; `context/formats/dispatch-metrics.md` specifies `met_{timestamp_ms}_{random6}` on the same pattern. These ids are IMMUNE TO RENUMBERING and are already cited across records. The convention is settled; the question is what else deserves one.
  - SESSION IDS have the same shape, `sess_{timestamp}_{random}`, minted at GATE IN and carried into commit bodies -- an existing durable join between a commit and the dispatch that produced it. Evaluate whether this already answers more of the problem than it appears to.
  - NAMED ARCHITECTURE DOCUMENTS under `docs/architecture/` are durable named anchors. Measured 2026-11-02, core ships six: `batch-admit-schema.md`, `extension-system.md`, `handoff-schema.md`, `orchestrate-cycle-postflight.md`, `orchestrate-state-machine.md`, `system-overview.md`. They are named, not numbered -- so cite them by name; there is no numeric decision-record id scheme here to extend.
  - Records in this system ALREADY cite decisions by durable name: route labels, numbered decisions inside a specific plan, document names, section headings.
THE DESIGN QUESTION IS WHETHER DECISIONS DESERVE FIRST-CLASS DURABLE IDS OF THAT KIND -- and if so, where they live, who mints them, and what cites them.

=== QUESTIONS THE RESEARCH MUST ANSWER, VERDICT-FIRST ===
(1) What is the MINIMAL durable identifier for a record, and for a DECISION made inside a record, given renumbering and two independent counters? "The existing minted-id convention, applied to X" is a better answer than a new scheme.
(2) Which existing fields ALREADY carry traceability, which are REDUNDANT, and what is GENUINELY MISSING? Prefer strengthening an existing field over minting a new one. `parent_task` is the obvious candidate to strengthen, since it already encodes lineage and is already validated.
(3) Does `specs/CHANGE_LOG.md` carry ANYTHING not recoverable from `specs/archive/` plus git history plus per-record artifacts? Evidence at filing suggests not: it is an archival log that stopped being written for a month across four archival runs with nobody noticing, which is itself evidence about how load-bearing it is. But VERIFY rather than assume.
  MEASURED 2026-11-02, exactly three files in the source store reference CHANGE_LOG, and nothing else does: `context/patterns/todo-archival-reference.md`, `skills/skill-todo/SKILL.md`, and the memory extension's `context/project/memory/knowledge-capture-usage.md`. Re-verify that set; it is small enough that retirement is cheap IF the verdict goes that way.
  RETIREMENT REQUIRES UPDATING A POINTER OUTSIDE THE SOURCE STORE. A consumer repository's `specs/ROADMAP.md` has a `## Maintenance` section stating that "the durable record is `specs/CHANGE_LOG.md` and `specs/archive/`" -- verified live. Retiring the file without fixing that sentence points readers at a durable record that no longer exists. Note that this pointer lives in a consumer repository, so it cannot be fixed by an edit under `agent-system/**`; the design must say how it is handled.
(4) WHO WRITES THE TRACEABILITY DATA, AND WHEN? A scheme that depends on an agent remembering to record a decision WILL DEGRADE EXACTLY AS CHANGE_LOG DID -- that degradation is the best-evidenced fact available here, so treat it as the primary design constraint rather than a caveat. Prefer a mechanism that FALLS OUT OF WORK ALREADY BEING DONE: something already written at a gate, already minted at dispatch, already committed.
(5) WHAT CONSUMES IT? Name the consumers concretely; a traceability scheme with no named reader is a cost with no benefit. The `/orient` record (`orient_command_with_scout_agent_retire_review`) reconstructs "what happened and why" BY HAND across precisely this scattered state -- its own description enumerates the same spread -- and is the obvious first consumer. RELATE THE DESIGN TO IT rather than duplicating it: /orient is read-only by construction and renders a brief to the user, so it is a reader of traceability data, never a writer of it.

=== HARD CONSTRAINTS ===
- THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS A RECORDED DESIGN WITH A VERDICT ON CHANGE_LOG, NOT A LANDED MECHANISM.
- RESPECT THE ADDITIVE-TO-REDUCTIVE RATIO. `systematic_script_and_test_corpus_efficiency` measured roughly SIXTEEN non-terminal records that add machinery against roughly THREE that reduce it, and concluded that working the backlog to completion makes the system larger. A design that adds a new file format, a new script AND a new gate to track work that git already tracks is THE WRONG ANSWER. "Strengthen two existing fields and retire one file" is a better outcome than any new subsystem.
- IF THE HONEST VERDICT IS THAT CURRENT MECHANISMS SUFFICE and only CHANGE_LOG's pointer needs fixing, THAT IS A COMPLETE AND SUCCESSFUL OUTCOME. Say so and stop. A refutation of the premise is a result, not a failure to deliver.
- Every existing-mechanism claim must be RE-VERIFIED against the live tree. Several figures in this description were measured on 2026-11-02 and will drift.

=== SEQUENCING: RECOMMENDATION ONLY, DELIBERATELY NOT A DEPENDENCY EDGE ===
No `dependencies[]` edge is declared onto the /todo consolidation record (`consolidate_duplicated_todo_implementation`), following this task space's own precedent that a recommendation is preferable to an edge that would overconstrain.

THE RECOMMENDATION: IF this design concludes that CHANGE_LOG should be KEPT AND WRITTEN, that writing behavior MUST NOT LAND IN /todo until the consolidation record has settled which /todo implementation is authoritative. The abandoned `todo_consolidate_and_optimize` record's phase-ordering rationale applies verbatim -- remove the divergence surface BEFORE new behavior lands on it. Landing a CHANGE_LOG writer into one of two divergent copies is how the current defect was created in the first place: the never-dispatched skill carries CHANGE_LOG stages that never run.

IF THE VERDICT IS RETIREMENT, there is no /todo behavior to land and NO INTERACTION with that record at all, which is why this is a recommendation rather than an edge.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===
- A recorded design answering (1) through (5), verdict-first.
- An EXPLICIT KEEP-OR-RETIRE VERDICT on `specs/CHANGE_LOG.md`, with the grounds that settled it stated plainly enough that a reader can disagree with the grounds rather than only with the conclusion.
- An explicit answer on the `task {N}:` commit convention, including "accepted and worked around" as a permitted answer with grounds.
- Every existing-mechanism claim re-verified against the live tree, with the measurement stated.
- NO IMPLEMENTATION in this record beyond what the design itself requires -- and if the design requires none, none.

=== DECLARED file_scope IS THE ARTIFACT DIRECTORY ONLY, DELIBERATELY ===
This record's file_scope names only its own `specs/` artifact directory. Every file named above --
`context/reference/state-management-schema.md`, `rules/git-workflow.md`,
`rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md`, `context/patterns/todo-archival-reference.md` and the
rest -- is an INPUT TO BE READ, not an edit target. A design record that declares its reading list
as territory manufactures collisions with every record that genuinely edits those files, and
`context/reference/state-management-schema.md` in particular is also in the /todo consolidation
record's scope, which would turn a deliberate non-edge into a shared-territory batching obligation
for no reason. IF the accepted design turns out to require edits under `agent-system/**`, WIDEN
file_scope at that point via `update-task-status.sh` and re-run the collision check -- do not edit
outside the declared scope silently.

artifacts.summary: Verdict-first design: KEEP specs/CHANGE_LOG.md unmodified (re-verified not stale, self-healing batch writer), accept-and-work-around the task {N}: commit convention (session_id already provides the durable join), no new field/file/script, and a documentation-only cross-record decision-citation convention (project_name slug + artifact round + Decision N) as the one genuine gap.
Three-phase plan: named citation convention in report-format.md plus pointers, recognized-optional Decisions heading for plans with validate-artifact.sh mirror, redeploy and full gate.

active_projects.description:
/tag's version-consistency gate is unpassable when a manifest version intentionally does not track release tags

SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never .claude/**, a disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). REDEPLOY AFTERWARDS via deploy-headless.sh.

ORIGIN: hit live on 2026-10-19 while tagging v0.4.32 in the PersonalWebsite repo. Duplicate check performed at creation time: a TODO.md + state.json scan for /tag and version-consistency returned only false positives (the substring "tag" inside "stage"). No existing task covers this.

== PROBLEM (reproducible on EVERY /tag invocation in PersonalWebsite) ==

skill-tag Step 3.5 "Validate Version Consistency" (SKILL.md line ~184) discovers any
pyproject.toml / setup.cfg / setup.py / package.json / Cargo.toml within maxdepth 3 of the repo
root, extracts its declared `version`, and HARD-FAILS when any one of them differs from the
computed tag. The gate has NO notion of a manifest whose version field is not the release version.

In PersonalWebsite, package.json is
  {"name":"benbrastmckie-website","version":"0.1.0","private":true}
-- an unpublished Astro site deployed to Cloudflare Pages. Under npm's own semantics a
`private: true` package is never published, so its `version` is inert: no consumer reads it.
Meanwhile that repo's vX.Y.Z tags are DEPLOYMENT markers (v0.4.32 reached today, 32 patch
deploys).

Evidence the two axes were never coupled (measured, re-verify before planning): iterating
`git show $c:package.json | jq -r .version` over every commit returned by
`git log --format=%h -- package.json` yields 0.1.0 for EVERY such commit. The declared version has
never once equaled a tag.

Consequence: the gate can never pass there, and BOTH resolutions it prints are wrong.
  - "Update the mismatched manifest(s) to 0.4.32, commit, then re-run /tag" invents a
    version-tracking convention for a field no consumer reads, and demands a dummy commit before
    every single deploy.
  - "--skip-version-check" must then be passed on every tag forever. A gate that permanently
    requires its own override carries zero signal and trains the user to pass the override
    reflexively -- which also disarms it in the repos where it WOULD be a real catch (a genuinely
    published package whose manifest drifted).

== ROOT FIXES TO EVALUATE -- research/plan must RULE on these, not assume ==

1. PREFERRED: treat `"private": true` in package.json as "this manifest declares no release
   version" and exclude it from the gate. Principled (it is npm's own semantics), needs zero
   configuration, and fixes the whole class of private-site repos at once. Handle the analogous
   idiom in the same pass: Cargo.toml `publish = false`.
   DO NOT "FIX" THESE -- already correct: pyproject.toml `dynamic = ["version"]` and Cargo
   `version.workspace = true` ALREADY yield empty from the existing extractors and are therefore
   already handled; SKILL.md's own inline comments say so explicitly.

2. GENERAL ESCAPE HATCH, complementary to 1 (NOT a substitute): an explicit per-repo opt-out for a
   manifest that intentionally diverges, since a NON-private manifest can still legitimately not
   track tags. Follow the existing `.syncprotect` precedent documented in CLAUDE.md (project root,
   one relative path per line, `#` comments, blank lines ignored) rather than inventing a new
   config shape.

3. WEAKER -- record as considered-and-rejected unless 1 and 2 both prove insufficient: infer intent
   from history, i.e. if the declared version has never equaled any existing tag, downgrade the
   gate from fatal to a warning. Rejected by default because it is implicit and silently weakens a
   real gate.

HARD CONSTRAINT on any chosen design: a genuinely published (non-private) manifest whose version
really HAS drifted from the computed tag MUST still hard-fail. Do not soften the gate into a
universal warning.

== SECONDARY DEFECT (same file, folded into this task deliberately -- shares one plan) ==

Step 3.6's changelog extraction (SKILL.md line ~344) is
  changelog_section=$(awk -v ver="$new_version_bare" '$0 ~ "^## \\[" ver "\\]" {found=1; next} ...')
The on-disk source store is CORRECT (verified: it reads `$0 ~ ...`). But when the skill body is
loaded WITH invocation arguments, the bare `$0` token is interpolated with those args -- the copy
actually executed on 2026-10-19 literally read
  --patch ~ "^## \\[" ver "\\]"
a corrupt awk program. `$*` and `$1` elsewhere in the same file survived intact, so the hazard is
specific to bare `$0`.

Any agent executing that snippet verbatim in a repo that DOES have a CHANGELOG.md would
mis-extract the section or error outright. PersonalWebsite only dodged it because it has no
CHANGELOG.md, so that branch never ran.

Fix direction: rewrite so no bare `$0` appears in skill-embedded bash. Note `index($0,...)` and
`match($0,...)` are equally exposed -- prefer a grep+sed formulation, or `{line=$0}` ONLY if that
form is itself verified safe under argument interpolation. Then audit the rest of the core
extension's skill-embedded bash for the same `$0` interpolation hazard.

Why this is one task, not two: both defects live in the same file (skill-tag/SKILL.md), both are in
the same /tag invocation path, both were found in one diagnosis, and both require the same
redeploy + the same single /tag verification run. Splitting them would mean two plans touching the
same file -- a serialized pair with no parallelism gained.

== EDIT TARGETS (source-store-deploy-boundary rule applies) ==

  agent-system/extensions/core/skills/skill-tag/SKILL.md
      Step 3.5 (line ~184), Step 3.6 (line ~344), and the Error Handling examples that mirror
      their output verbatim
  agent-system/extensions/core/commands/tag.md
      flag table + Requirements section, kept in sync with the skill

Confirmed at creation time: `grep -rln "skip-version-check"` over the source store matches exactly
these two files. The gate is inline bash in SKILL.md, not a separate script, so there is NO
scripts/ file to change.

== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ==

- `/tag --patch` in PersonalWebsite passes the version-consistency gate with NO override flag and
  NO package.json edit.
- A mismatch in a genuinely published (non-private) manifest still fails fatally.
- The gate's informational "no declared version found" path and both `--skip-*` disclosure paths
  keep working, including under `--dry-run` (all three sit before the dry-run exit).
- commands/tag.md documents whatever new opt-out mechanism lands.
- No bare `$0` remains in skill-embedded bash in skill-tag/SKILL.md; the rest of the core
  extension's skills are audited for the same hazard and findings recorded.

Severity: blocking-in-practice for /tag in any private-manifest repo (the gate cannot pass without
a permanent override), plus a latent correctness bug in Step 3.6 for any repo with a CHANGELOG.md.

Retire routing_agents_hard in favour of hard_contracts across books, cslib and lean, then remove the ladder rung and gate16

ORIGIN: surfaced by an /orchestrate batch-gate run as an unattributed gate16 finding ("lean still declares routing_hard/routing_agents_hard"). Backlog reconciliation found NO existing task covering it: the gate-framework task and the gate20 eager-load-budget task each explicitly name it "known pre-existing and out of scope", and no other open task mentions hard_contracts at all. gate16's own header comment in verify-deploy.sh names this work as "the one remaining follow-on".

== WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE TODAY (measured, re-verify before planning) ==

- routing_hard is fully dead: NO manifest in the source store declares it. gate16 and the schema guide still name it defensively.
- routing_agents_hard is declared by THREE source extensions, not two: books, cslib AND lean. gate16's header comment says "cslib/lean" and undercounts by one. Each declares only research + implement (plan parity is deliberately not required).
    books: {research:{books:"books-research-hard-agent"}, implement:{books:"books-implementation-hard-agent"}}
    cslib: {research:{cslib:"cslib-research-hard-agent"}, implement:{cslib:"cslib-implementation-hard-agent"}}
    lean:  {research:{lean4:"lean-research-hard-agent"}, implement:{lean4:"lean-implementation-hard-agent"}}
- NO manifest anywhere declares hard_contracts yet. The migration target key does not exist in any manifest.
- Only lean is currently deployed, so gate16 reports ONE hit; deploying books or cslib would surface two more. The warning count understates the real scope.
- routing_agents_hard is genuinely still consulted: command-route-agent.sh line ~69 resolves it as the first rung of a three-rung ladder (routing_agents_hard -> routing_agents -> core default). Removing the declarations without replacing the behaviour would silently downgrade every --hard dispatch in these three domains to its standard agent with no contract injection.

== THE CENTRAL DESIGN POINT, STATED SO IT IS NOT MISREAD ==

This is NOT a key rename and NOT a value migration. Per context/guides/manifest-routing-schema.md, the two keys are unrelated and differently shaped:
  routing_agents_hard  two-level {op:{task_type: agent_name}}  -> resolves WHICH AGENT is dispatched
  hard_contracts       one-level {task_type: [contract_paths]} -> resolves WHICH CONTRACT FILES are injected into a --hard dispatch prompt, via routing_lookup_flat() in orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh Stage 3.5

The intended end state is that --hard stops dispatching separate "-hard" agents and instead dispatches the STANDARD agent with the domain's behavioural contracts injected. Verify that premise against the schema guide and the six existing -hard agent bodies BEFORE planning; if the -hard agents carry behaviour that contract injection cannot express, say so and stop rather than forcing the migration.

== SCOPE ==

1. Decide and record whether each of the six -hard agents reduces to standard-agent + injected contracts. This is the gating question; everything below depends on a yes.
2. Author hard_contracts declarations for books, cslib and lean.
3. Remove routing_agents_hard from all three manifests; retire the six -hard agent files if step 1 rules they are redundant.
4. Remove the routing_agents_hard rung from command-route-agent.sh and its lib, and Check C from lint-routing-wiring.sh (which enforces routing_agents_hard internal completeness).
5. Remove gate16 from verify-deploy.sh and its gate-registry.data row; decide separately whether a replacement gate asserting the ABSENCE of both keys is worth keeping.
6. Update context/guides/manifest-routing-schema.md, which is the authoritative description and currently documents routing_agents_hard as surviving.

== VERIFY ==

- No source manifest declares routing_hard or routing_agents_hard.
- A --hard dispatch in each of the three domains still receives its behavioural contracts, demonstrated per domain, not asserted.
- lint-routing-wiring.sh passes with Check C removed and no remaining reference to it.
- Full gate set passes with gate16 gone and no new findings.

Severity: minor-to-costly. Nothing is broken today -- gate16 WARNS and never fails, and the ladder works. The cost is a standing warning that makes every full-gate reading noisier, three manifests carrying a key documented as slated for removal, and a documented follow-on that nothing tracks.

# Proposed task: audit cross-extension duplication of the bounded-wait agent contract

## GOAL

Rule on whether the bounded-wait MUST/MUST NOT bullet pair (the agent-contract prohibition
against ending a turn to await a harness completion notification for a backgrounded local
verification/gate/build/test process) should be inherited from one canonical place instead of
restated as a literal copy in every carrying implementation agent file, and -- separately --
confirm whether any carrying agent's own surrounding prose contradicts the bullet pair the way
the lean extension's two implementation agents previously did.

## CORRECTED FRAMING (settled by a prior task; do not re-litigate the premise)

A prior task fixed the lean extension's two implementation agents
(lean-implementation-agent.md, lean-implementation-hard-agent.md), which had instructed the
forbidden detach-then-await-a-notification shape in direct contradiction to
core/agents/general-implementation-agent.md's Local Long-Running Command Discipline. That task's
own research found the OTHER ~14 implementation agents already carry the canonical bounded-wait
bullet pair correctly and already PASS both of lint-agent-contracts.sh's relevant checks (Check H
for bullet-pair presence, Check K for absence of the forbidden shape in surrounding prose). So
the open question for THIS task is **propagation architecture** -- one canonical source kept in
sync by a lint versus 14+ independently-maintained literal copies -- not an unfixed defect
requiring per-file repair. Do not frame this task's starting point as "~18 files may each carry a
divergent copy of the wait rule"; that framing was the prior task's own starting assumption and
was falsified by its research.

## STANDING CONSTRAINT (why literal copies exist at all)

An `@`-reference inside an agent body does NOT auto-resolve when Claude Code spawns a subagent.
This is why `agent-system/extensions/core/context/patterns/bounded-build-waiter.md`'s own
"Canonical Agent-Contract Bullet (Generated-Copy Source)" section is a generated-copy source
read by a human or a lint script, not an `@`-import: each in-scope agent body must carry a
literal copy of the bullet text, and `lint-agent-contracts.sh` Check H keeps every copy in sync
by comparing it against that source file. Any inheritance design this task proposes must either
work within this constraint (e.g. a build/deploy-time text-injection step that still leaves a
literal copy in the file the subagent actually reads) or justify overriding it with evidence that
subagent spawning now resolves `@`-references (it does not, as of this writing).

## TWO DECISIONS THE PRIOR TASK ALREADY MADE (binding on this task)

- The two lean implementation agents now carry the canonical bullet pair verbatim and are listed
  in lint-agent-contracts.sh's `BOUNDED_WAIT_IN_SCOPE_RELATIVE_PATHS` (Check H) like every other
  in-scope agent. Do not propose removing them from that array.
- `lint-agent-contracts.sh`'s `CHECK_K_EXCLUDED_RELATIVE_PATHS` array is now EMPTY (previously
  held the two lean paths as a time-boxed, now-discharged exclusion). The
  `is_excluded_from_await_notification` helper and the empty array remain in place so a future,
  differently-reasoned exclusion has a home -- this task may add a new exclusion to it if it
  finds a genuine case, but must not treat the empty array itself as unfinished work.

## REPRODUCE COMMANDS (carried forward so this task never re-derives them)

Check H's own re-audit command (from its comment block (c) in lint-agent-contracts.sh):
```
cd agent-system/extensions && for f in $(find . -name '*implementation*agent.md' | sort); do
  echo "$(grep -c run_in_background "$f") $(grep -c bounded-build-waiter "$f") $f"; done
```

Check K's own occurrence-set command (from its comment block in lint-agent-contracts.sh):
```
grep -rc 'completion notification' agent-system/extensions/*/agents/*.md
```

## WHAT THIS TASK SHOULD PRODUCE

- A ruling, recorded as a decision with rationale, on whether to keep the literal-copy-plus-lint
  model as-is, add a build/deploy-time generation step that still lands a literal copy, or some
  other mechanism -- not a vague "investigate" outcome.
- If the ruling changes the propagation mechanism: an implementation plan is a separate,
  subsequent step; this task's own scope is the ruling plus whatever minimal demonstration proves
  the chosen mechanism works for at least one agent file, not a full ~14-file migration in one
  pass.
- Confirmation (via the reproduce commands above, re-run fresh rather than trusted from this
  description) of which agents currently carry the bullet pair and which do not, since the set
  may have drifted since this description was written.

## NON-GOALS

- Re-litigating the lean extension's own fix (already completed, already verified green via
  lint-agent-contracts.sh and the regression suite `test-lint-agent-contracts-await-notification.sh`).
- Extending this contract to research agents -- `bounded-build-waiter.md`'s own "Item 4 Ruling:
  Research Agents Are Out of Scope Here, Not Dismissed" already rules that out of THIS
  mechanism's scope as a separate, explicitly deferred follow-up; this task may note it but
  should not fold it in.

## FILE SCOPE (expected; confirm and set precisely at plan time)

- agent-system/extensions/core/context/patterns/bounded-build-waiter.md
- agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/lint/lint-agent-contracts.sh
- Whichever agent file(s) are chosen for the minimal demonstration, if the ruling changes the
  propagation mechanism.

Map core's Verification Tier vocabulary onto Lean build scopes in the lean extension, so a non-final lean phase stops declaring a whole-project build without naming what requires it.

THE OBSERVED COST (BimodalLogic repo, 2026-10-15, measured from .lake/build-guard.stdout on a full guarded build): four implement dispatches in one batch each ran a full unscoped lake build at every phase boundary. One such build rebuilt 414 of 2848 jobs for 6354s of elaboration; Metalogic was 5649s of that across 306 modules; SubformulaProperty.lean alone was 1103s. Lake is already incremental, so this is not lake rebuilding everything -- it is the whole-project build being invoked repeatedly.

WHAT IS ALREADY IN PLACE, AND MUST BE REUSED RATHER THAN REBUILT. core/context/formats/plan-format.md already defines the entire mechanism this task needs:
  - **Verification Tier:** (required per phase) one of prose, local, interface, full (L97-98).
  - **Tier Justification:** (required on every NON-FINAL phase, omitted on the final phase) -- one sentence naming the specific covering check for a tier below full, OR "the specific cross-cutting surface no cheaper tier covers" for a non-final full (L103-107, L314).
So core already requires a non-final phase to justify choosing full. The gap is not a missing rule. The gap is that the lean extension never says what prose/local/interface/full MEAN in terms of Lean build scope, so lean plans default to full with no meaningful justification and the existing core requirement does no work.

SCOPE. Add to the lean extension a mapping from core's four tiers to concrete Lean verification actions -- for example which tiers are satisfied by lean_goal plus lean_verify, which by `lake build Module.Name` for the modules the phase touched, and which require the whole-project build plus the build-enabled gates. State it once, in the shared flow document both lean implementation agents already reference (context/project/lean4/agents/lean-implementation-flow.md), and have the agent files point at it rather than restating it.

DO NOT DECIDE THE PHASE-COMMIT QUESTION HERE. Whether a phase COMMIT is gated on a full build is owned by the task named in this task's dependencies, which revises three files on exactly that point and carries a measured counterexample: a module-scoped build of Periodic.lean passed while the full library build failed, because a new `dualStructure` clashed with `WeakCanonical.dualStructure` in another module. A scoped build cannot see cross-module name clashes or downstream breakage. This task must ADOPT whatever that task settles, not relitigate it. Hence the dependency edge: run after it, and write the tier mapping to match its conclusion.

THE POINT THAT SURVIVES EITHER OUTCOME. If that task concludes every non-final lean phase genuinely needs the full build for cross-module clash detection, then that conclusion belongs in the tier mapping ONCE, as the standing cross-cutting surface, rather than being re-justified ad hoc in every lean plan -- and plan authors should then declare full with a pointer to it. If instead some phases can be covered more cheaply, the mapping says which and how. Either way the outcome is that a lean plan's tier declaration carries information instead of being a reflex.

PRESERVE, these are not up for weakening: every lake build stays DETACHED via Bash(run_in_background: true) routed through lake-build-guard.sh, and the bounded-wait obligation in context/project/lean4/operations/external-process-wait and long-builds guidance is unchanged. long-builds.md is explicit that a single module can exceed the foreground cap and that a scoped build is never exempt from either obligation. Also preserve the checks that genuinely need a complete build: check-module-invariants.sh in build-enabled mode and the olean-freshness-for-every-touched-module tier.

NON-GOALS. Do not modify lake-build-guard.sh. Do not modify core/context/formats/plan-format.md -- core already carries the required fields and this task consumes them rather than changing them. Do not decide the phase-commit gating question. Do not touch any deployed .claude/ tree: the source store under agent-system/extensions/ is the edit target and a redeploy follows.

ACCEPTANCE. A tier-to-Lean-action mapping stated once in the shared lean flow document, with the two lean implementation agent files pointing at it and not contradicting it; the mapping consistent with whatever the dependency task settled about phase-commit gating; the detachment, guard and bounded-wait obligations verifiably unchanged; no task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/.

active_projects.title: Refactor the books extension's context corpus against the settled convention: role-scoped loading, agent-set review, version-pinned files
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET (agent-system/extensions/books/..., never .claude/**). `.claude/` is a
gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store; a file hand-authored there
is silently wiped by the next deploy. See rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md.

No task-number references in any file written into the source store
(rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md). Cite durable anchors -- filenames, section headings,
decision numbers -- instead. Task numbers are permitted in this description and in specs/**.

== PROSE PRECONDITION (not a dependency edge) ==

This task refactors against the SETTLED record, not the one in flight. Before it runs, the consuming
repository ~/Projects/Logos/Verification must have landed its alpha review of the book convention WITH
THE VERSION STAMPED. If the review has not landed, this task waits -- refactoring the corpus against a
record still being revised buys a second refactor.

== GOAL ==

The books context corpus is 21 files, about 4,450 lines, WRITTEN BEFORE THE SPLIT AND BEFORE THE ALPHA
REVIEW. Review it against the settled record and refactor it so each books agent loads EXACTLY THE CONTEXT
ITS JOB NEEDS, with the AGENT SET ITSELF reviewed and EVERY FILE PINNED to the convention version.

== THE MEASURED STARTING POINT ==

  - `index-entries.json` (538 lines, 21 entries): only `project/books/README.md` and
    `patterns/signal-tagging.md` carry `load_when.task_types: ["books"]` -- AND NO REAL CONSUMING-REPO TASK
    CARRIES TYPE `books` (measured: fourteen books-topic tasks are `lean4`, two `general`, one `typst`).
    The other 19 entries are on-demand with empty `task_types`. NOTHING IS KEYED BY ROLE.
  - Corpus line counts: `README.md` 88; `domain/` known-gap-register 275, layer-vocabulary-and-matrix 230,
    book-toml-v2 187, certificate-ledger-and-records 275, identity-and-versioning 237,
    status-and-trust-vocabularies 163, gate-tiers 194; `patterns/` authoring-workflow 213,
    warning-driven-convergence 174, gate-collision-ledger 198, signal-tagging 204, books-review-submode 219,
    books-revise-submode 288; `standards/` metadata-split 180, forgery-probe-discipline 171,
    reconciliation-contract 231, observation-record 249; `tools/` tooling-inventory 213,
    typst-template-contract 244, certify-guide 214.
  - FIVE domain files restate Decisions 2, 3, 7, 8, 9, 11 and 12, which after the split are SINGLE FILES OF
    70 TO 330 LINES WITH STABLE ANCHORS. Before the split, restating Decision 7 saved an agent from
    ingesting a 359 KB file; after it, that decision is a short file at a stable path, so the
    restatement's REMAINING value is only whatever it ADDS.
  - FOUR agents split by LIFECYCLE PHASE (research 188, research-hard 295, implementation 294,
    implementation-hard 285 lines), NOT BY JOB.

== THE FIVE JOBS, MEASURED ==

| Job | Files needed today | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| Author a book | layer-vocabulary-and-matrix, metadata-split, book-toml-v2, authoring-workflow, warning-driven-convergence, rules/books.md | ~1,050 |
| Certify / diagnose | gate-tiers, gate-collision-ledger, certify-guide, tooling-inventory, forgery-probe-discipline | ~990 |
| Document a book | typst-template-contract, reconciliation-contract, status-and-trust-vocabularies | ~640 |
| Maintain the record | the record-editing guardrail rule and maintenance pointer, identity-and-versioning, known-gap-register | ~580 |
| Review / revise the convention | observation-record, signal-tagging, books-review-submode, books-revise-submode | ~960 |

Nothing in the extension selects by job. A research dispatch that reads the corpus README is pointed at all
of it.

== FIVE DELIVERABLES ==

(1) A PER-FILE REVIEW TABLE, all 21 files: what it RESTATES, what it ADDS BEYOND THE DECISION FILE MEASURED
IN LINES, which job needs it, and a disposition -- KEEP / TRIM TO THE DELTA / MERGE / RETIRE INTO THE RECORD
/ SPLIT BY ROLE. "Lines that are not in the decision file" is a measurement, not a judgement; make it.

(2) A LOADING MATRIX for the five jobs, giving each agent and skill an EAGER SET and an ON-DEMAND SET,
expressed in `index-entries.json` `load_when` keys and in each agent's context references, with a
PER-DISPATCH EAGER BUDGET MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER.

(3) THE AGENT-SET RULING: which jobs need their own agent and which are served by EXISTING agents given a
role-specific context slice -- including whether the existing typst and planner agents already cover
documenting and planning -- with the frontmatter and routing-table changes that implement it.

(4) A `- **Reviewed against convention version**:` HEADER ON EVERY CORPUS FILE, matching the extension pin,
plus THE RULE THAT A BUMP OBLIGES RE-REVIEW of every file whose header is BELOW the pin. This turns "update
all the parts" from a search into a list.

(5) Registration (`README.md`, `EXTENSION.md`, `index-entries.json`, `manifest.json`), the gate suite green,
and A STATED MEASUREMENT THAT NO DISPATCH KIND'S EAGER CONTEXT GREW.

== BINDING PREFERENCES AND PROTECTED FILES ==

PREFER TRIMMING TO THE DELTA over retiring a file, unless the delta is empty. PREFER A ROLE-SPECIFIC
CONTEXT SLICE over a new agent, unless the slice would exceed the budget for an existing agent's other jobs.

These carry MEASURED FAILURE MODES THE RECORD DOES NOT HAVE and MUST SURVIVE: `gate-collision-ledger`
(the six gate collisions), `forgery-probe-discipline`, `warning-driven-convergence` (the `book_requires`
loop), and `certify-guide` (the certifier's economical operation) -- along with the `Books.+` glob failure
and the `certificate/` directory discovery corruption these files record.

Deleting the corpus and pointing agents at the record directly was considered; it is REJECTED AS AN
ASSUMPTION and must instead be MEASURED per file, precisely because of those failure modes.

== OWNER GATE ==

The owner looks at THE LOADING MATRIX DURING PLANNING, BEFORE the rewrite. Role separation is a design
choice, not a mechanical consequence of the measurements.

== SCOPE BOUNDARY ==

NO change to the record. NO change to `/books` sub-mode SEMANTICS beyond their context references. NO
repo-side files. Applying the same loading-matrix method to the lean4 and typst corpora is a possible later
task, NOT this one.

== ACCEPTANCE ==

The review table covers all 21 files with measured deltas and a disposition each; the loading matrix names
an eager and on-demand set per job with before/after budgets; the agent-set ruling is recorded with reasons;
every corpus file carries the version header and the bump rule is stated; the four protected files survive;
no dispatch kind's eager context grew, stated as a measurement. Gate: `verify-deploy.sh`,
`check-extension-docs.sh`, `check-task-references.sh`, and the books test suites.

== DEPENDENCIES ==

Depends on the books-extension split-retarget task (the retargeted anchors and the version pin every corpus
header must match) and on the record-editing guardrails task (the rule and maintenance pointer that the
"maintain the record" job's eager set loads).

Seed report: specs/342_refactor_books_context_corpus_role_scoped/reports/01_seed-books-context-engineering.md
