ORIGIN: Conclusion stage (channel b, agent-system changes) of an /orchestrate invocation over BimodalLogic:#761 (ladder realization theorem), user-approved at the lead level and dispatched to the meta builder for task creation only. FILED HERE, NOT IN BIMODALLOGIC: an agent-system change belongs in the repository that owns the source store, per the mis-siting correction recorded under this repo's #390 and the authoring hole recorded under #391. All issue-log citations below are entry_ids in the ORIGINATING repository's log, BimodalLogic:specs/761_ladder_realization_theorem/issues.jsonl -- the identifier #761 is a BimodalLogic number and does NOT resolve in this repository's state.json. Cross-repo overlap has no mechanical representation today (#401); where it matters below it is stated in prose.

CITATIONS -- two independent cases, two different gates, six days apart:
  BimodalLogic:#761:iss_1791769990070_9Nl16r  (class gate-baseline, severity minor, implement, dispatch_seq 3) -- the repo-wide task-reference lint.
  BimodalLogic:#761:iss_1792364282512_jWKKvT  (class verification-criterion, severity minor, implement, dispatch_seq 6) -- the vacuous-definition grep.
A third entry in the same log (iss_1791770495965_TM78BN) records the vacuous-pattern case a second time from the earlier phase, so the grep case recurred across dispatches rather than being a one-off.

PROVENANCE OF THE FIGURES BELOW: every file, line number, and quoted string in the ROOT CAUSE sections was re-derived by direct read of the source store at creation time (2026-10-18), not copied from the originating report. Line numbers move -- re-derive before editing. The incident narratives and measured costs are CARRIED-UNVERIFIED from the cited issues.jsonl entries; they are not re-measurable from this repository, since the incidents happened in BimodalLogic.

LIVE SYMPTOM -- a plan demanded an absolute gate result the tree cannot produce, so a correctly-passing phase had to report a non-conforming verdict:
(a) "repo-wide check-task-references.sh --quiet exits 0". MEASURED: it exits 1 on 198 pre-existing occurrences in Boneyard/*/README.md (archived code), NONE in any file the task touched; every touched file passes individually and the per-file checks pass. The criterion is unattainable without an out-of-scope archive cleanup.
(b) "vacuous-definition grep count 0", asserted repeatedly across phases. MEASURED: the tree carries one PRE-EXISTING hit at HEAD -- FormalSystem/Examples/TemporalStructures.lean:495, int_domain_universal -- whose `:= trivial` closes a REAL goal (membership in the universal domain is True by definition). So the hit is not even a finding; it is a correct declaration that matches the pattern.
Both had to be reported as baseline-unchanged rather than as the stated criterion. The cost is not a wrong result -- it is that a conforming phase produces a verdict that does not match its own plan, which is indistinguishable on first read from a phase that failed its gate, and so costs a triage pass and erodes the verdict's meaning.

ROOT CAUSE -- the authoring standard has every adjacent rule except this one. Verified in the source store at creation time (around these lines; re-derive before editing):
- context/formats/plan-format.md's `### Naming a tool's entry point in verification criteria` (around line 498) is the closest existing rule and is strikingly near-miss. It MANDATES naming the repository's sanctioned entry point rather than a bare binary, and it MANDATES checking the invoked command's exit status rather than relying on a stdout diff against a baseline -- because "a tool broken identically on both sides of that diff makes 'no new findings' vacuously true". So the file already reasons about baselines, and already warns about one specific way a baseline-relative criterion goes wrong, while never stating when a criterion MUST be baseline-relative in the first place. Its declared enforcement level is advisory prose only, with no corresponding validate-artifact.sh check.
- `### Counts-are-hypotheses obligation` (around line 422) makes any count, file list, or scope estimate a hypothesis carrying a `**Scope Hypothesis**:` line stating how to confirm it at implementation time. That is the right shape for a FORWARD-LOOKING estimate; a standing pre-existing finding count is a different object -- a measurable property of HEAD that should be measured ONCE at plan time and then held fixed as the comparison point.
- `## Verification Tiers` (around line 260) defines how BROADLY verification must run (prose < local < interface < full) and requires the final phase to take the `full` tier, whose in-phase verification is "the complete gate set for the repository". So the format compels a repo-wide run at the final phase while saying nothing about how to phrase the criterion for a repo-wide gate that is not green at HEAD. The two halves do not meet.
- A grep of plan-format.md for baseline / pre-existing / unchanged finds only incidental uses: the stdout-diff warning above, and tier prose using 'unchanged' in an unrelated sense. There is no rule to amend here -- there is a rule to ADD, sited next to the entry-point rule it completes.

SCOPE -- add the baseline-relative criterion rule to plan-format.md, sited as a sibling of `### Naming a tool's entry point in verification criteria`, and propagate it to the planner's own contract. The rule must state at least:
- WHEN it binds: whenever a phase's verification criterion invokes a gate whose scope exceeds the phase's edit scope (a repo-wide lint, a tree-wide grep, an aggregate sweep) AND that gate is not green at the task's starting commit.
- WHAT the criterion must then say: a baseline-relative verdict -- 'no NEW findings relative to the recorded baseline', or 'baseline-unchanged at N' -- never an absolute 'exits 0' or 'count is 0'.
- WHERE the baseline comes from: measured at PLAN time against the task's starting commit and recorded IN the plan, so the implementer compares against a number the plan committed to rather than one it discovers mid-phase and could rationalize. Pair this with the existing counts-are-hypotheses and carried-figure obligations rather than restating them.
- The ESCAPE HATCH, stated explicitly: an absolute criterion remains correct and preferred when the gate IS green at the starting commit, and a plan may legitimately demand an absolute result as a deliberate in-scope cleanup -- in which case the cleanup is part of the task's scope and must appear in a phase's Files to modify.
Then rule on enforcement: whether validate-artifact.sh can mechanically flag an absolute criterion naming a known repo-wide gate, or whether this stays advisory prose like its sibling rule. Record the ruling either way; a mechanical check here is only worth having if it can avoid false-flagging the legitimate absolute case above.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
- Do NOT make this a license to lower a gate. 'No new findings' must mean the gate still RUNS at full repo scope and its exit status is still checked -- the sibling entry-point rule is explicit that a stdout-diff-only comparison makes 'no new findings' vacuously true when the tool is broken identically on both sides. Whatever wording lands must preserve that warning and must not be satisfiable by a diff alone.
- Do NOT restate the carried-figure or counts-are-hypotheses conventions. report-format.md's `## Carried-Figure Discipline` is the authoritative home for carried figures for BOTH reports and plans, and plan-format.md already POINTS there rather than restating, deliberately so the two cannot drift. A recorded baseline figure is a measurement this plan makes, so say how it interacts with those conventions and point; do not fork them.
- Keep every existing heading string in plan-format.md unchanged; several have consumers (validate-artifact.sh, plan-file-scope-harvest.sh reads `Files to modify`, and the lean-gated `## Lean Challenge Statements` section).
- If a mechanical check is added, it MUST fail open and advisory-first. A false flag on a legitimate absolute criterion would push planners toward vaguer criteria, which is worse than the defect being fixed.

VERIFY:
- If a validate-artifact.sh check lands: extend scripts/tests/test-validate-artifact.sh with both polarities -- an absolute criterion over a repo-wide gate is flagged; an absolute criterion over a gate that is green at HEAD, and one paired with an in-scope cleanup phase, are NOT flagged.
- Pin that the existing `### Naming a tool's entry point in verification criteria` and `### Counts-are-hypotheses obligation` sections are intact and that plan-format.md still points to report-format.md for carried figures rather than restating it.
- Use the two cited cases as the acceptance fixtures: a criterion phrased the new way must be satisfiable by the measured states described above (198 archived occurrences untouched; one pre-existing correct declaration matching the vacuous-definition pattern).
- Do NOT verify by running the full verify-deploy.sh aggregator while other sessions are active -- use the scoped narrowing.

TERRITORY EDGES:
- 447 (SERIALIZATION plus a SEMANTIC edge): also writes agents/planner-agent.md, scripts/validate-artifact.sh and its test, and it is the record that AMENDS the carried-figure convention this rule must point at rather than fork. Reconcile wording during research; it should land first so this record points at the amended convention.
- 446 (SERIALIZATION only): also writes context/formats/plan-format.md (and plan-file-scope-harvest.sh, which parses that file). Same file, disjoint section -- it works the Files-to-modify/file_scope reconciliation half.
- 385 (SERIALIZATION only): also writes context/formats/plan-format.md, in the lean-gated `## Lean Challenge Statements` section. Disjoint section, direct file collision.
- 328 (SERIALIZATION only, OPERATOR-LIFTABLE): covers core/context/, core/agents/ and lean/rules/ at DIRECTORY level as part of a net-deletion corpus consolidation. Liftable with update-task-status.sh --depends-on-remove if an operator confirms it does not touch these files.
- 360 (SERIALIZATION only, LOW CONFIDENCE): also writes scripts/validate-artifact.sh, for an advisory CARRIED-UNVERIFIED well-formedness check. Only relevant if this record adds a validate-artifact.sh check; if the enforcement ruling is 'advisory prose only', lift it.

DUPLICATE CHECK PERFORMED. 447 is the nearest neighbour and is flagged for reconciliation rather than treated as disjoint: it strengthens the discipline around a figure a plan REPEATS from another record, while this record governs how a criterion a plan AUTHORS must be phrased against a measured starting state. Related, complementary, not the same object. 420 (plan-size versus cycle-budget mismatch) and 313 (advisory lint for hand-authored batch proposals) are both plan-authoring adjacent but address sizing and batching, not criterion phrasing. No absorption candidate found.

ADDITIONAL TERRITORY EDGES, SURFACED MECHANICALLY BY validate-state.sh AFTER THIS RECORD WAS WRITTEN (declared with labelled rationale rather than as bare numbers, per the open concern that dependency edges conflate semantic and serialization rationale -- see #438):
- 435 (SERIALIZATION only, OPERATOR-LIFTABLE): declares agent-system/extensions/core/context/ and core/agents/ coarsely, covering this record's plan-format.md and planner-agent.md targets.
- 448 (SERIALIZATION only, OPERATOR-LIFTABLE): declares agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/ coarsely, covering test-validate-artifact.sh.
ALL EDGES IN THIS PARAGRAPH ARE SERIALIZATION-ONLY AND OPERATOR-LIFTABLE. They exist because the OTHER record declares a coarse directory rather than because this record's targets are contested; validate-state.sh flags each as a "Coarse file_scope declaration" warning against that other record. An operator who confirms the predecessor does not touch this record's named files may lift any of them with update-task-status.sh --depends-on-remove.

========================================================================
TWO FURTHER CASES FOLDED IN 2026-11-04 (backlog reconciliation at proposal time, not a redundancy
pass). The conclusion stage of an /orchestrate invocation over BimodalLogic:#833 (stab definable
from open modals) audited two proposed agent-system tasks against this backlog via
scripts/audit-task-proposals.sh, found this record already owns the obligation, and folded the new
evidence here instead of filing a duplicate. Citations are entry_ids in the ORIGINATING
repository's log, BimodalLogic:specs/833_stab_definable_from_open_modals/issues.jsonl -- the
identifier #833 is a BimodalLogic number and does NOT resolve in this repository's state.json.
Both narratives are CARRIED-UNVERIFIED from that log; they are not re-measurable here.

FURTHER CASE (c) -- iss_1793830921380_pXdFr7, class documentation, severity COSTLY, phase research,
dispatch_seq 1. A dispatch's verification gate required that check-module-invariants.sh "must be
green". Re-measured at baseline: it exits 1 for a PRE-EXISTING C16 unusedArguments finding on
RaySummary.mem_cellAt_of_shift_of_hasForwardSlack in LadderChain.lean, unrelated to the dispatched
work, while INV, both C15 assertions and C2 all PASS. The criterion was unsatisfiable as written and
the gate had to be read PER-CHECK rather than by script exit code.
WHY THIS IS NOT JUST A THIRD INSTANCE: cases (a) and (b) above are both gates with a standing
FINDING COUNT, where "no new findings relative to the recorded baseline" is the natural wording.
This gate is a multi-check AGGREGATOR whose single exit code conflates independent checks, so a
count-based baseline does not express it -- the operable form is per-check assertion ("INV, C15 and
C2 PASS; C16 baseline-unchanged"). The wording this record adds must therefore cover BOTH shapes, or
it will leave the aggregator case without a sanctioned phrasing. Nothing above currently does.

FURTHER CASE (d) -- iss_1793830921344_wcU6Ej, class documentation, severity minor, phase research,
dispatch_seq 1. The INVERSE failure, from the same baseline measurement. A widely-repeated dispatch
note stated that check-metalogic-cycles.sh currently exits 1 for a pre-existing eighth-upward-edge
reason. Re-measured at baseline: it exits 0, printing "PASS upward import set is exactly the
recorded 8 line(s)". The note was stale, and the staleness inverted the correct reading -- under the
true baseline a nonzero exit is a NEW failure, which the stale note would have had an implementer
dismiss as pre-existing.
This is the direct argument for this record's "WHERE the baseline comes from" clause, and it
sharpens it: a baseline inherited as DISPATCH PROSE decays silently and in the dangerous direction
(toward dismissing real failures), whereas a baseline measured at plan time against the task's
starting commit cannot. State that asymmetry in the rule rather than only requiring plan-time
measurement, so the reason the prose route is forbidden survives in the text.

FOLDED IN 2026-11-04 -- THE SCOPING FACILITIES ALREADY EXIST; NAME THEM RATHER THAN IMPLYING A
TOOL GAP. Absorbed from a duplicate record in the BimodalLogic task space that this record
strictly supersedes: BimodalLogic:#835 plan_format_baseline_relative_gate_criteria carried the
same generic provision, cited all three of the originating entry_ids named above, and declared a
SUBSET of this record's own file_scope. That record is now abandoned with a durable pointer here.
The identifier #835 is a BimodalLogic number and does NOT resolve in this repository's state.json.
The paragraph below is the one thing it held that this record did not.

MEASURED at that record's creation and CARRIED-UNVERIFIED here -- re-confirm both facilities still

WHY THIS BEARS ON THE WORDING, NOT JUST THE EVIDENCE: the provision this record adds EXTENDS

mechanism and must not be written as though one were needed -- a reader who concludes a tool gap

active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/literature/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). ORIGIN: Conclusion stage (channel b, agent-system changes) of an /orchestrate invocation over BimodalLogic:#761 (ladder realization theorem), user-approved at the lead level and dispatched to the meta builder for task creation only. FILED HERE, NOT IN BIMODALLOGIC: an agent-system change belongs in the repository that owns the source store, per the mis-siting correction recorded under this repo's #390 and the authoring hole recorded under #391. All issue-log citations below are entry_ids in the ORIGINATING repository's log, BimodalLogic:specs/761_ladder_realization_theorem/issues.jsonl -- the identifier #761 is a BimodalLogic number and does NOT resolve in this repository's state.json. Cross-repo overlap has no mechanical representation today (#401); where it matters below it is stated in prose.

CITATION: BimodalLogic:#761:iss_1791766528048_mRmvAU -- class 'tooling bug or gap', severity minor, phase research, dispatch_seq 1, resolution 'worked_around'.

PROVENANCE OF THE FIGURES BELOW: every file, line number, and quoted string in the ROOT CAUSE sections was re-derived by direct read of the source store at creation time (2026-10-18), not copied from the originating report. Line numbers move -- re-derive before editing. The incident narratives and measured costs are CARRIED-UNVERIFIED from the cited issues.jsonl entries; they are not re-measurable from this repository, since the incidents happened in BimodalLogic.

LIVE SYMPTOM -- `literature-search.sh` returned degraded=true with NO results for a quasimodel query, and the research agent fell back to grepping the corpus source directory directly for the specific theorem and definition numbers it needed. The workaround succeeded, so nothing was lost on this run; what the entry records is that the agent had to invent the fallback, because the tool told it retrieval had degraded and then told it nothing about what to do next.

ROOT CAUSE -- the degraded signal is produced honestly and then dropped in exactly the case where it is most actionable. Verified in the source store at creation time:
- scripts/literature-search.sh computes `degraded = fallback_tier != 'bm25'` and emits it in the result envelope alongside fallback_tier and query_error. Its own comment states the intent precisely: degraded is "the honest, never-silent signal that distinguishes 'retrieval degraded' from 'genuine zero-result', which literature-briefing.sh consumes downstream". The producer is correct and this record does not fault it.
- When the merged result set is EMPTY, that same code sets `fallback_tier = 'none'`, which makes `degraded` TRUE. So the zero-result case is reported as degraded by construction -- which is the honest reading (no tier answered), but it also means degraded=true with zero results is the single most common degraded shape, not an edge case.
- scripts/literature-briefing.sh is the consumer, and its degraded banner is emitted under the guard `if [ "$degraded" = "true" ] && [ "${#briefing_lines[@]}" -gt 0 ]`. The second conjunct is the defect: the banner requires that there BE results. It carries three well-written variants -- a trigram-fallback warning, a phrase-retry warning after an FTS5 syntax error, and a generic fallback_tier warning -- and each ends by telling the agent to verify relevance itself, which is advice that only makes sense when rows exist.
- Net: in the cited case (degraded=true, fallback_tier='none', zero rows) the briefing emits NO banner and NO directive at all. The signal the producer went to trouble to make never-silent is silent precisely when the agent has nothing else to go on.

SCOPE -- give the zero-result degraded case its own banner and a usable directive, in literature-briefing.sh. The directive should say what the agent in the cited incident worked out by itself, so the next agent does not have to:
- distinguish 'the corpus has nothing on this' from 'the index did not answer this query', and say which one the tool can and cannot tell apart;
- name the sanctioned next steps rather than leaving them to invention -- at minimum re-querying with narrower or alternative terms (the --multi mode exists for per-term recall in one process), consulting --toc / --doc to navigate by document structure instead of ranking, and, as the explicit last resort, reading the corpus source directly;
- state whether an index-health problem is indicated and where that is checked (`/literature --validate`, and the index-health mode of `/literature`).
Also rule on whether `fallback_tier = 'none'` on an empty result set should remain folded into `degraded`, or be reported as its own distinguishable state. Do not change the producer's semantics without recording the reasoning: downstream consumers read the field, and the current definition is deliberate.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
- Preserve the three existing banner variants verbatim in their current cases (trigram_fallback, phrase_retry, generic). This record ADDS a fourth case; it does not rewrite the working ones.
- Preserve backward compatibility of the envelope reader. literature-briefing.sh already accepts a legacy bare-array shape and two envelope shapes; whatever lands must keep all three readable and must not fail when degraded/fallback_tier/query_error are absent.
- `query_error` is a DIFFERENT condition from `degraded` -- the producer documents it as non-null only when every sub-query failed against every database that exists. A genuine query error must not be collapsed into the new zero-result banner; if anything it deserves a louder one.
- The banner is guidance, not a gate. Nothing here may make a research dispatch fail or block on degraded retrieval.
- No task-number references in the banner text or the context file -- it lands under agent-system/**.

VERIFY:
- Add a literature/scripts/tests/ case covering the cited shape: degraded=true, fallback_tier='none', zero rows -> a banner and a directive ARE emitted. Pin the negative too: a healthy bm25 answer with rows emits NO banner.
- Pin that each of the three existing variants still fires in its own case with its existing wording.
- Pin that all three accepted envelope shapes still parse, including the legacy bare array with no degraded field.
- Reproduce the cited case end-to-end if the corpus allows: a query that no tier answers should now produce actionable text rather than silence.

TERRITORY EDGES:
- 328 (SERIALIZATION, NOT liftable without a read): its file_scope names literature/scripts/literature-search.sh EXPLICITLY (not merely by directory) and also covers literature/scripts/tests/ at directory level, as part of a net-deletion corpus consolidation. This is a direct, named collision on one of this record's own files, so the edge stands until an operator reads 328's plan and confirms otherwise.
- 437 (NO EDGE, checked explicitly): also a literature-extension record, but its file_scope is the Zotero export/search path (zotero-generate-export.sh, zotero-search.sh, zotero-export-status.sh, zotero-export-freshness.sh, tools/zotero-scripts.md). Disjoint files and a disjoint mechanism -- a false-negative acquisition answer from a lossy sqlite reconstruction, not a dropped retrieval-health banner. Both concern honest reporting of a degraded literature answer, so keep the wording consistent, but neither blocks the other.

DUPLICATE CHECK PERFORMED. No open task names literature-briefing.sh. 404 (completed, literature) was checked. 437 is the only adjacent open literature record and is explicitly ruled disjoint above. No absorption candidate found.

active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/{formal,lean}/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Resolve source_dir from <project-root>/.claude-extensions.json and edit at the path mirroring the deployed one. REDEPLOY AFTERWARDS via deploy-headless.sh to RESULT=landed_verify_clean. No task-number references in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md) and no record-versioning language (rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

GOAL. Repository-specific content from one consuming Lean project has leaked into the SHARED agent-system source store, so every other repository deploying the formal or lean extension receives context files asserting facts about a Lean tree it does not have. Resolve the four affected files, choosing PER FILE between relocation and de-specialization, and record the grounds that settled each choice.

THE ROUTE DECISION IS DELIBERATELY NOT PRE-MADE. See the PER-FILE ROUTE DECISION section below. A dispatch that quietly defaults to one route for all files has not done the work this record asks for.

STANDING INSTRUCTION: re-verify every path, line number and hit count below against the tree before citing it again. They were measured at filing and they drift.

=== WHAT WAS MEASURED (2026-11-02, at HEAD 86b8fc759) ===

Pattern `FormalSystem|BimodalLogic|BimodalTools|ProofChecker|PlusLanguage`, counted over TRACKED files in the source store (`git ls-files agent-system/`). Hit counts are matching LINES, not occurrences.

The four substantive files:

- agent-system/extensions/formal/context/project/logic/domain/frame-constraint-landscape.md -- 37 hits. Line 5 states the coupling outright, verbatim: "Every Lean name below is fully qualified and lives in the ProofChecker (BimodalLogic) tree."
- agent-system/extensions/formal/context/project/logic/domain/ztime-no-finite-carrier-fmp.md -- 26 hits. The same coupling is stated at line 16: "qualified and lives in the ProofChecker (BimodalLogic) tree or in the named probe file."
- agent-system/extensions/lean/context/project/lean4/domain/sentence-translation-contract.md -- 17 hits. Hardcodes FormalSystem/SourceLanguage/Sentence.lean, BimodalTools/SentenceExport.lean and Tests/BimodalTest/ paths.
- agent-system/extensions/lean/context/project/lean4/domain/ladder-counter-observables.md -- 1 hit, at line 10, naming FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/RaySummary/LadderModel.lean. Likely a trivial de-specialization.

CONSEQUENCE: the formal and lean extensions ship these files to every consumer. A repository with no such Lean tree receives domain context whose named declarations and paths do not exist for it, and nothing currently detects this.

=== PER-FILE ROUTE DECISION -- NOT PRE-DECIDED, BY EXPLICIT RULING AT FILING ===

Two routes are on the table for each of the three substantive files. The implementer must choose PER FILE and record the grounds that settled it. The choice may legitimately differ per file.

ROUTE A -- RELOCATE. Move the file out of the shared store into the consuming repository's own per-repo context location, context/repo/, which is never overwritten by a deploy and is protected by that repository's .syncprotect (which already protects context/repo/project-overview.md). COST: whatever generic value the file carries for other Lean projects is lost to them.

ROUTE B -- DE-SPECIALIZE IN PLACE. Keep the file in the shared store, strip repository names and hardcoded paths, rewrite as generic guidance. COST: more work, and it risks discarding the concrete grounding that makes the file useful at all. A file whose every claim is a specific Lean declaration may not survive de-specialization as anything a reader can use.

Neither route is pre-selected and neither is the default. For frame-constraint-landscape.md and ztime-no-finite-carrier-fmp.md in particular, note that their own opening lines ANNOUNCE the coupling rather than hiding it -- weigh whether that is a file honestly declaring its scope (favouring Route A) or a fixable framing (favouring Route B).

=== TRIAGE INVENTORY -- THE FULL SWEEP, NOT JUST THE FOUR ===

active_projects.title: Rule on and close the V7 refusal of a positive directory pathspec for a git rm --cached untracking whose content is still on disk
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Edit at the path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

ORIGIN: Conclusion stage (channel b, agent-system changes) of an /orchestrate invocation in the Logos/Vision consumer repository, user-approved at the lead level and dispatched to the meta builder for task creation only. FILED HERE, NOT IN VISION: an agent-system change belongs in the repository that owns the source store. Cross-repo overlap has no mechanical representation today (see the open record on cross-repo source-store gate blindness); where it matters below it is stated in prose.

CITATION: the sole evidence base is Vision:#234:iss_1793752881502_Y429oi, in the ORIGINATING repository's log at Vision:specs/234_resolve_standing_verify_deploy_gate_failures/issues.jsonl. The identifier #234 is a Vision number and does NOT resolve in this repository's state.json. No suggested_channel hint was recorded on that entry; routing it to the agent-system channel is the orchestrator's own classification. Severity: minor -- a workaround exists and nothing is blocked.

PROVENANCE: every file, line number, and quoted string in the ROOT CAUSE section below was re-derived by direct read of the source store at creation time (2026-11-03), not copied from the originating report. Line numbers move -- re-derive before editing. The incident narrative and the exit code are CARRIED-UNVERIFIED from the cited entry, which states they were reproduced in a dedicated scratch reproduction rather than observed once in situ; that reproduction is not re-runnable from this repository.

LIVE SYMPTOM. In the Vision consumer repo, `git rm -r --cached .opencode` was run to untrack a stale deploy tree (500 files; the index records deletions, every file remains on disk because `--cached` by definition leaves the working tree alone). The subsequent `git-commit-scoped.sh` invocation naming `.opencode` as a positive pathspec exited 2 with the V7 refusal.

ROOT CAUSE, VERIFIED AGAINST THE SCRIPT (not inferred). In scripts/git-commit-scoped.sh, the post-add verification loop over `add_positive_pathspecs` (around lines 844-878) first tests `git ls-files --error-unmatch -- "$p"`. For an untracked-by-`--cached` directory this fails, because no file under it remains in the index. Control then reaches the `staged_deletion_adds` carve-out, whose acceptance predicate is the three-way conjunction

    [ ! -e "$p" ] && [ "$staged_deletion_rc" -eq 1 ] && git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD

The second and third conjuncts hold: `git diff --cached --quiet HEAD -- .opencode` exits 1 (a staged change exists) and HEAD exists. The FIRST conjunct fails -- `.opencode` is still on disk. The path therefore falls through to `genuinely_failed_adds+=("${p} (not present in the index at all)")` and the refusal at the `genuinely_failed_adds` block below it. The carve-out's own comment states its premise explicitly: it exists for "the source half of a directory move", where the content is GONE from the working tree. A `--cached` untracking inverts exactly that premise -- index deletions WITH content present -- so it matches neither the normal staged-path branch nor the sanctioned fully-staged-deletion branch.

WORKAROUND ACTUALLY USED, AND WHY IT IS NOT A FIX. The implementing agent temporarily relocated `.opencode/` out of the repository, invoked `git-commit-scoped.sh` directly with the same pathspec set, then restored the content immediately after the commit landed. It deliberately did not use `git-commit-phase.sh`, whose post-commit `files_touched` completeness check would have misreported the restored untracked content as dirty. No forbidden git operation was used at any point. This manoeuvre is undocumented and fragile, which is the entire cost being reported: an untracking commit currently requires relocating files out of the working tree.

PRIOR ART -- DO NOT RE-LITIGATE ANY OF IT. (a) The completed record fixing the V2 gate dropping staged deletions addressed a DIFFERENT gate and a different mechanism, and its premise is again "content gone from both working tree and index"; it does not cover this case. (b) The settled bare-directory-pathspec policy and its lint (scripts/lint/lint-directory-pathspec-boundary.sh and its test) are closed; do not reopen the policy itself. (c) Both specs/state.json and specs/archive/state.json were scanned at creation time for `--cached`, `staged_deletion`, and untracking subjects: no open or closed record covers the `--cached`-with-content-present case. (d) No open record names scripts/git-commit-scoped.sh or scripts/tests/test-git-commit-scoped.sh in its file_scope.

THE TENSION THE PLANNER MUST RULE ON EXPLICITLY, NOT ASSUME AWAY. rules/git-workflow.md's Git Safety section (around lines 89-92) forbids a directory-or-glob `git add` pathspec outright and has that forbiddance enforced by hooks/guard-destructive-git.sh via exit 2 on a dirty tree. Yet a directory pathspec is ROUTINE inside git-commit-scoped.sh: context/standards/git-staging-scope.md (around line 423) records that the sanctioned path for staging `${task_dir}/` is precisely to invoke git-commit-scoped.sh, "because its own internal `git add` runs as a subprocess, never as the literal top-level `tool_input.command` the hook observes", and V7's own carve-out sanctions a directory pathspec for the source half of a directory move. So "a directory pathspec was used, therefore the refusal is correct" is NOT an adequate disposition of this report. Rule on which of these the untracking case is, and record the ruling with its reasoning:
  (1) it belongs INSIDE the existing fully-staged-deletion carve-out (widen the predicate's first conjunct);
  (2) it needs its OWN narrower carve-out, kept distinct from the directory-move case so neither's premise is blurred; or
  (3) it should not be served by a carve-out at all, and instead by a documented explicit-file-list recipe for untracking.
A defensible outcome here is (3) -- "no widening, and here is the recipe instead". Do not widen by default.

REQUIRED OUTCOME REGARDLESS OF THE RULING. An agent must be left with a sanctioned, documented way to commit an untracking WITHOUT relocating files out of the repository. If the ruling is (3), the recipe is the deliverable and the script may be left unchanged apart from a refusal message that points at it.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
- Do NOT weaken V7 into a boolean. The script's own comment documents that the `git diff --cached HEAD` exit code is read EXACTLY -- 1 means "a staged change exists", 0 means "nothing staged here" (a genuine drop), and anything above 1 (notably 128) is a git error such as an out-of-repo pathspec. Only 1 is accepted, specifically so the out-of-repo hard failure keeps refusing. Any predicate change must preserve that discrimination; a `! git diff ...` boolean test would wrongly accept the 128 case.
- Do NOT let a widened predicate accept a genuinely-unstaged directory. The whole point of V7 is that a path present on disk and differing from the index is a real failure. If the first conjunct is relaxed, something else must establish that every tracked file under the pathspec is staged as deleted -- content presence alone must not become sufficient.
- Keep the two deletion shapes distinguishable in the NOTE output. The existing note names its paths as "the source half of a directory move"; an untracking is not that, and a note that conflates them makes a future reader mis-diagnose.
- Preserve the existing gitignore-advisory tolerance and the `add_exclude_pathspecs` handling in the same loop; neither is in scope to change.

VERIFY:
- Extend scripts/tests/test-git-commit-scoped.sh with a regression case that FAILS against the current script and passes after the fix: a `git rm -r --cached <dir>` whose content remains on disk, committed via a positive directory pathspec.
- Pin the existing fully-staged-deletion directory-move case in the same suite, so the fix is demonstrated not to regress the carve-out that already works.
- Pin the two cases the predicate must keep refusing: a path present on disk with unstaged content differences, and an out-of-repo pathspec (the 128 case).
- Use the scoped narrowing (scripts/tests/run-all.sh --only SUITE), not the full aggregator.

TERRITORY EDGES (labelled rationale rather than bare numbers):
- 430 (SEMANTIC and SERIALIZATION): owns scripts/git-commit-phase.sh, scripts/tests/test-git-commit-phase.sh, and context/standards/git-staging-scope.md. Semantic because the workaround narrative above turns on git-commit-phase.sh's post-commit `files_touched` completeness check misreading restored untracked content as dirty -- if the ruling produces a recipe that routes through git-commit-phase.sh, that check is the thing it must not trip. Re-read this record against what 430 lands.
- 446 (SERIALIZATION, with a doc-territory edge): owns context/standards/git-staging-scope.md and scripts/git-commit-phase.sh as part of the plan-to-file_scope reconciliation work. Any recipe this record documents in git-staging-scope.md is contested territory with it; land after it and merge rather than overwrite.
- 328 (SERIALIZATION only, OPERATOR-LIFTABLE): declares agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/ at directory level as part of a net-deletion corpus consolidation, covering test-git-commit-scoped.sh.
- 435 (SERIALIZATION only, OPERATOR-LIFTABLE): declares agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/ at directory level, covering both of this record's script files.
- 448 (SERIALIZATION only, OPERATOR-LIFTABLE): declares agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/ at directory level, covering test-git-commit-scoped.sh.
The three edges marked OPERATOR-LIFTABLE exist because the OTHER record declares a coarse directory, not because this record's targets are contested; an operator who confirms the predecessor does not touch this record's named files may lift any of them with update-task-status.sh --depends-on-remove.

DUPLICATE CHECK PERFORMED. Nearest neighbours are 430 and 446, both of which own git-commit-phase.sh and git-staging-scope.md. Both were considered as absorption targets and rejected: neither names git-commit-scoped.sh, and neither's subject is the V7 post-add verification predicate. The completed V2 staged-deletion record and the closed directory-pathspec policy records are ruled disjoint above with reasons.

CROSS-REPO CITATION CAVEAT: the issue identifier cited below is an entry in a DIFFERENT repository's issue log -- BimodalLogic, at specs/849_forward_slack_discharge_and_exact_shift_iteration/issues.jsonl. The number 849 is a BimodalLogic task number and does NOT resolve in this repository's state.json; do not try to look it up here. This record is filed here, not in BimodalLogic, because an agent-system change belongs in the repository that owns the source store. Cross-repo overlap has no mechanical representation today; that gap is itself tracked by this repo's cross_repo_source_store_gate_blindness task.

CITATION: BimodalLogic:849:iss_1793754709802_bWVZnZ (class `tooling`, severity minor, implement phase).

=== THE DEFECT ===
`lean-challenge-snapshot.sh --check` has no scope limit, so a compiled research prototype parked under `specs/**` -- the sanctioned place for one -- forces a false ambiguity failure and exit 71 on a tree that is in fact correct.

=== ROOT CAUSE, RE-DERIVED BY DIRECT READ OF THE SOURCE STORE AT FILING (line numbers drift; re-derive before editing) ===
`do_check()` begins ~L198. It resolves each pinned identifier by walking the entire project root:
  - `find_lean_files(root)` (~L273-279) is `os.walk(root)` with `dirnames` filtered to exclude only the directory names ".git", ".lake" and "lake-packages".
  - The comparison loop (~L282-294) iterates that walk over `project_root` and skips exactly one further path, the pinned Challenge artifact itself (`challenge_abs`).
Any other `.lean` file anywhere in the tree is therefore a comparison target, including `specs/{NNN}_{slug}/prototype/*.lean`. When such a prototype declares a pinned name, `ambiguous` (~L297) is non-empty and the branch at ~L306-310 writes "ERROR: '{n}' resolves to more than one declaration in the current tree: {files}" and exits 71.

=== A SECOND ENUMERATION SITE -- DERIVED HERE, DO NOT FIX ONLY ONE ===
The R2 fallback path has its own independent enumeration and its own ambiguity hard-exit:
  - ~L602: `tree = git("ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", commit)`; ~L605: `lean_files = [p for p in tree.stdout.splitlines() if p.endswith(".lean")]`. That is every `.lean` path in the repo tree at that commit with NO exclusions at all -- not `.lake`, not the Challenge.
  - ~L652-660: `ambiguous` non-empty writes "ERROR: R2 fallback found more than one declaration named '{n}' at commit {commit[:12]}: {files}. Extraction ambiguity is a hard error, never a best-effort guess." and exits 71.
So a COMMITTED prototype under `specs/` reaches the same defect by the second path. If a scope notion is introduced, both sites should consume it rather than diverging; if only `--check` is fixed, the record must say why. The R2 site's "hard error, never a best-effort guess" stance is deliberate and must be preserved for genuine ambiguity.

=== MEASURED INCIDENT (carried from the originating repo's record; CARRIED-UNVERIFIED in this repository -- re-derive or re-cite at plan time) ===
Five of seven pinned names resolved to two declarations each: the landed declaration in `FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/RaySummary/LadderChain.lean` and the research prototype `specs/849_.../prototype/helpers-compiled.lean`. The implementer checked drift independently (whitespace-normalized header diff of all seven against Challenge.lean: MATCH 7/7) and did NOT edit the prototype, correctly treating it as the research record. The verdict is advisory by the script's own header, so nothing was blocked. The loss is that a mechanical check was silently replaced by a manual one.

=== DESIGN QUESTION -- DELIBERATELY NOT PRE-DECIDED ===
Candidate mechanisms, each with a real cost to weigh:
  (a) Exclude `specs/` in the enumeration. Cheapest, but hard-codes a repository-layout assumption and would also hide a genuine duplicate that some task legitimately parks under `specs/`.
  (b) An explicit `--scope` / `--include` flag. Pushes the decision out to every call site, and the call sites include a hook.
  (c) Read the task's own `file_scope`. Couples the script to state.json's `file_scope`, whose lifecycle is owned elsewhere in this repo (see the file-scope-lifecycle topic).
Research picks one and says why the others lose.

=== INVARIANT TO PRESERVE ===
Two declarations of a pinned name in the LIBRARY is a real finding and must remain a hard failure. The deliverable narrows WHERE the script looks, never WHETHER genuine ambiguity fails.

=== EXIT-CODE CAUTION ===
Prefer not to overload 71 further. This script's exit-code vocabulary is already being revised by the zero-goal task named in dependencies, which observes that 71 is documented as "Config error" in the script's own header while carrying several distinct conditions. Adopt whatever that task settles rather than inventing a parallel code.

=== DEPENDENCIES AND WHY (serialization against shared file territory, NOT absorption) ===
Both descriptions were read in full at filing; neither covers `--check`'s identifier resolution or its tree-walk scope, so this is a sibling record, not a duplicate.
  - `lean4_plan_with_zero_lean_goals`: same two lean files. Owns the exit-71 vocabulary for the EXTRACT step and the zero-theorem plan shape. A new scope mechanism must not reintroduce a 71 collision that task is in the middle of untangling.
  - `snapshot_lean_challenge_at_plan_time`: same two lean files plus the test suite. Owns WHEN the snapshot is invoked (moving it to plan time). Changing where `--check` looks while the invocation point is moving would land two uncoordinated edits in one script.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===
(a) A `--check` run in a tree containing a `.lean` prototype under `specs/{NNN}_{slug}/` that declares a pinned name resolves to the library declaration and exits 0.
(b) Two declarations of a pinned name in library source still fails hard.
(c) Both enumeration sites either share the scope notion, or the record states why only one is in scope.
(d) The chosen mechanism documented in `challenge-snapshot.md` and in the script's own exit-code header.
(e) Test coverage in `scripts/tests/test-lean-challenge-snapshot.sh` for both (a) and (b).

=== NON-GOALS ===
Do not relitigate the advisory-vs-blocking status of the `--check` verdict. Do not change drift detection (the whitespace-normalized header comparison) itself. Do not touch a deployed `.claude/` tree.

active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: resolve `source_dir` from <project-root>/.claude-extensions.json and edit at the path mirroring the deployed one. Never hand-author under a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store (rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). REDEPLOY AFTERWARDS. CROSS-REPO CITATION CAVEAT: the issue identifier cited below is an entry in a DIFFERENT repository's issue log -- BimodalLogic, at specs/849_forward_slack_discharge_and_exact_shift_iteration/issues.jsonl. The number 849 is a BimodalLogic task number and does NOT resolve in this repository's state.json; do not try to look it up here. This record is filed here, not in BimodalLogic, because an agent-system change belongs in the repository that owns the source store. Cross-repo overlap has no mechanical representation today; that gap is itself tracked by this repo's cross_repo_source_store_gate_blindness task.

CITATION: BimodalLogic:849:iss_1793752926544_AfZmP9 (class `tooling`, severity minor, implement phase).

=== THE DEFECT ===
An empty `goals_after` from `lean_goal` means "no goals remain at this position". It is not the claim "this declaration elaborates". Nothing in the lean extension says so, while the shared flow document instructs the agent to verify STEP completion with exactly that tool.

=== MEASURED INCIDENT (carried from the originating repo's record; CARRIED-UNVERIFIED in this repository) ===
`lean_goal` returned an empty `goals_after` at a closing `exact` line whose term referenced an unknown constant (`Bool.true_ne_false`). The elaboration error surfaced only in the full `lake build`.

=== THE GAP, RE-VERIFIED IN THE SOURCE STORE AT FILING (line numbers drift; re-derive before editing) ===
  - `context/project/lean4/tools/mcp-tools-guide.md` ~L83 is the whole of what the guide says about this output: "- Omit `column` to see `goals_before` (line start) and `goals_after` (line end)". No trust-surface caveat.
  - `context/project/lean4/agents/lean-implementation-flow.md` ~L117: "**Verify step completion** with `lean_goal` (proof state) and `lean_verify` (axiom/sorry check); do NOT run `lake build` per-step". ~L151 restates it ("Per-step verification uses `lean_goal` + `lean_verify`"), and ~L113 leans on it again after each edit.
  - A grep of the whole lean extension for an empty-goals / not-evidence statement returns nothing. The only "not evidence" statements present concern other surfaces entirely: `operations/long-builds.md` on an unfinished build, and `domain/metadata-trust-surfaces.md` on an empty `meta_imports`.
So the agent is told to verify step completion with a tool whose trust surface is undocumented, and has no stated reason to distrust an empty goal list between phase boundaries.

=== WHAT THIS DOES NOT REVISIT (verified, not assumed) ===
The mitigation already exists: the completed task `lean_phase_commit_full_build_and_plan_anchor` gated a phase COMMIT on the full library build rather than a module-scoped one. That ruling stands and is not reopened. This task adds the missing statement about the tool itself, which is what makes the per-step instruction safe to follow BETWEEN those commit boundaries.

=== SUGGESTED SHAPE (research may refine) ===
State the trust surface ONCE and have consumers point at it. Two siting candidates:
  (a) Alongside the existing `goals_after` bullet in `mcp-tools-guide.md`.
  (b) In `context/project/lean4/domain/metadata-trust-surfaces.md`, which already exists for exactly this genre of "what this metadata is not checked by" statement and already carries a structurally identical sentence about an empty `meta_imports`; the guide would then need a pointer to it.
Pick one. Do not write it twice. The flow document's step-verification line should POINT at the statement rather than restate it.

=== A SUBSTANTIVE QUESTION WORTH ANSWERING, NOT JUST A CAVEAT ===
Say what the agent should do INSTEAD at step granularity, given that a per-step `lake build` is forbidden by the same line that names `lean_goal`. Candidates include `lean_diagnostic_messages` for the edited file (which reports elaboration errors, where `lean_goal` reports only goal state) and `lean_verify` on the fully qualified name. State the cheapest check that actually covers the unknown-constant case. A caveat with no replacement check leaves the agent with nothing to do differently.

=== DEPENDENCY AND WHY (serialization against shared file territory, NOT absorption) ===

Its own description names "which tiers are satisfied by lean_goal plus lean_verify" as an example of what it will state. active_projects.title: Make a plan's per-phase line estimates checkable against a line ceiling the same plan cites, so a plan cannot contradict its own arithmetic
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: resolve `source_dir` from <project-root>/.claude-extensions.json and edit at the path mirroring the deployed one. Never hand-author under a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store (rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). REDEPLOY AFTERWARDS. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description, which lives under specs/**.

CROSS-REPO CITATION CAVEAT: the issue identifier cited below is an entry in a DIFFERENT repository's issue log -- BimodalLogic, at specs/849_forward_slack_discharge_and_exact_shift_iteration/issues.jsonl. The number 849 is a BimodalLogic task number and does NOT resolve in this repository's state.json; do not try to look it up here. This record is filed here, not in BimodalLogic, because an agent-system change belongs in the repository that owns the source store. Cross-repo overlap has no mechanical representation today; that gap is itself tracked by this repo's cross_repo_source_store_gate_blindness task.

CITATION: BimodalLogic:849:iss_1793754003650_RvAmat (class `plan-scope drift`, severity minor, implement phase).

=== THE DEFECT ===
A plan's per-phase line estimates can sum past a line ceiling the same plan cites, while the plan simultaneously asserts it stays under that ceiling. Nothing catches the contradiction at plan time.

=== MEASURED INCIDENT (carried from the originating repo's record; CARRIED-UNVERIFIED in this repository) ===
Per-phase line estimates of 110+120+95+10+90+80+130 against a 959-line starting file sum to roughly 1594, past the 1500-line `longFile` limit the plan itself cited, while the plan's own Rollback/Contingency note asserted the file "stays well under 1500". The file crossed 1500 at Phase 6. The implementer applied the originating repository's sanctioned remedy (its `LEAN_STYLE_GUIDE.md` "The long-file baseline" and `MODULE_INVARIANTS` C30): `set_option linter.style.longFile N` after the module docstring, N kept inside the linter's tight window and re-tightened per phase. No statement and no decomposition changed, so the cost was one in-flight deviation to record, not rework.

=== THE GAP IS NOT A MISSING FIELD -- RE-VERIFIED IN THE SOURCE STORE AT FILING (line numbers drift; re-derive before editing) ===
`core/context/formats/plan-format.md` already carries both the carrier field and the obligation:
  - ~L101-102: "**Scope Hypothesis:** (conditional -- required whenever the phase asserts a count, an enumerated file list, or a scope estimate)".
  - ~L424-428, "### Counts-are-hypotheses obligation": "Any count, file list, or scope estimate asserted in a plan is a hypothesis requiring implementation-time confirmation, never a fact." The same section states that the implementation-side gate which mechanically checks a confirmation happened is "a separate, out-of-scope concern for this document -- this section defines the planner-side carrier field only."
A per-phase line estimate IS a scope estimate, so it is already governed. What is NOT governed is the relation BETWEEN those estimates and a ceiling the same plan cites. Scope Hypothesis points each estimate forward at implementation-time reality, one phase at a time; nothing compares the estimates to each other, and nothing notices that their sum contradicts a limit the plan quotes in its own prose. The defect is internal inconsistency at plan time, which no amount of implementation-time confirmation catches any earlier.

=== THE DELIVERABLE IS SELF-CONTRADICTION, NOT ESTIMATE ACCURACY ===
A per-phase line estimate is inherently approximate and this task must not try to make it accurate. The target is narrower and fully decidable: a plan that (i) cites a numeric line ceiling and (ii) carries per-phase estimates of the same quantity must not also assert it stays under that ceiling when its own numbers say otherwise.

=== DESIGN QUESTION -- DELIBERATELY NOT PRE-DECIDED ===
Whether this is an authoring rule, a mechanical check, or a planner-agent checklist item is this task's decision. Weigh:
  (a) An authoring rule only. Cheapest, but the incident IS an author not doing the arithmetic, so a rule asking for the same arithmetic again is weak.
  (b) A mechanical check in `core/scripts/validate-artifact.sh`. This is the existing plan-format validator consumer: it already splits a plan into per-phase blocks and extracts per-phase field values (its per-phase Verification Tier check does exactly this), it already has an advisory-first warn-not-error convention with a documented promotion criterion, and it is non-blocking at every call site -- all of which suits a check over approximate numbers. The real cost: free-prose line estimates and a prose-quoted ceiling are not currently structured fields, so a check needs either a parse heuristic or a new field, and a new required field has its own cost across every plan author.
  (c) A planner-agent checklist item. Weakest and least durable; record it with its reason rather than passing over it.
Prefer reusing the existing carrier field and the existing consumer over inventing a new field or a new script, unless research shows neither can carry it.

=== GENERALITY REQUIREMENT ===
State the rule in terms of ANY numeric ceiling a plan cites against a per-phase quantity it estimates, not in terms of the Lean `longFile` linter. The incident came from a Lean repository, but `plan-format.md` is a core format document and must not acquire a Lean-specific clause. The `longFile` case may appear as a worked example only.

=== DUPLICATE CHECK PERFORMED AT FILING ===
Searches of this repository's `specs/state.json` (96 active tasks) and `specs/archive/state.json` for `longFile`, `long.file`, "line estimate" and "line budget" returned nothing in either. No absorption candidate. Independently, no existing task names `core/scripts/validate-artifact.sh` together with a cross-phase arithmetic concern.

=== TERRITORY NOTE (no dependency edge warranted) ===
`plan-format.md` is high-traffic: several unstarted tasks name it in file_scope under other topics (the orchestrator, core-agent-system and file-scope-lifecycle topics each have at least one). None of them touches the counts-are-hypotheses section or any line-estimate arithmetic, so no edge is warranted on substance. That file's contention set drifts, so re-check contention at plan time rather than trusting this sentence.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===
A stated rule, sited once, under which a plan citing a numeric ceiling and carrying per-phase estimates of the same quantity cannot assert conformance against its own arithmetic; a recorded decision among (a)/(b)/(c) with the rejected options stated on their own merits; if a mechanical check is chosen, it reuses `validate-artifact.sh` and its advisory-first convention rather than adding a script, and its findings stay advisory until that file's documented promotion criterion is met; the rule phrased generally, with `longFile` at most an example.

=== NON-GOALS ===
Do not attempt to improve line-estimate accuracy. Do not add a blocking gate over approximate numbers. Do not introduce a Lean-specific clause into a core format document. Do not touch a deployed `.claude/` tree.

=== THE TWO ACTUAL COARSE OVERLAPPERS, NAMED (measured at filing via validate-state.sh) ===
Both of this record's files sit under directories that two repo-wide sweeps declare at
directory granularity, so the validator reports a nominal overlap with each:
  - `reword_dead_lifecycle_command_prose_per_class` declares `agent-system/extensions/core/context/`
    and `agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/`, which contain both of this record's files.
  - `systematic_script_and_test_corpus_efficiency` declares `agent-system/extensions/core/context/`.
Neither names `plan-format.md` or `validate-artifact.sh` anywhere in its own description, and
neither is substantively about plan arithmetic -- the first rewords prose naming three deleted
lifecycle commands, the second consolidates the script and test corpus. No dependency edge is
warranted on substance, and serializing behind a declaration the validator itself flags as coarse
would be the wrong trade. ONE REAL RESIDUAL RISK worth checking at plan time rather than assuming:
the prose-rewording sweep would legitimately touch `plan-format.md` if that file names one of the
deleted lifecycle commands. Grep it before editing; if it does, coordinate instead of racing.

active_projects.title: check-record-versioning.sh PATH_SCOPE mode reports false-clean on a file present on disk but not git-tracked
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/ (never .claude/**, a disposable deploy artifact -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Edit at the path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh.

## Goal

check-record-versioning.sh PATH_SCOPE mode must never report clean for a file it did not actually scan.

## The defect, as observed

PATH_SCOPE mode enumerates its candidate set via `git ls-files PATH_SCOPE`. For a file that exists on disk but is not yet git-tracked, that enumeration returns zero rows, and the lint then reports CLEAN -- with no [SKIP] line and no diagnostic of any kind. The scan silently did nothing and said everything was fine.

## Why this is costly, measured

This false-clean caused a real near-miss in the write-time hook work. The new hook validate-no-record-versioning.sh carried the literal phrase "supersedes v1" in its own header prose while describing the rule it enforces. A Phase-1 scoped self-check over the new file reported clean -- because the file was not yet git-tracked. The violation was caught only later, by a full-repo scan, after which the header was rephrased and re-verified. Had it shipped, the hook would have blocked every future edit to its own source file: a self-blocking gate.

The general shape is worse than this one instance. Every caller that lints a file it has just created, before committing it, gets a clean verdict that means nothing. That includes exactly the self-hygiene checks a new blocking hook most needs.

## Required outcome

An untracked-but-present file within PATH_SCOPE is either scanned on its merits or loudly skipped. Silence is not an acceptable third option. If scanning untracked files is judged wrong (e.g. to avoid scanning build output), the skip must be explicit and visible on stderr, naming the file and the reason, so a caller can tell "clean" from "not examined".

Consider whether sibling lints that use the same git ls-files enumeration share the defect; if they do, say so and name them rather than fixing this one in isolation.

## Acceptance

A file that exists on disk, is not git-tracked, and contains a BLOCKING-tier occurrence does not yield a clean verdict from PATH_SCOPE mode. A fixture covering exactly that case is added to test-check-record-versioning.sh.

## Provenance

Derived from the orchestration conclusion stage, issue-log entry iss_1793754137229_u9DTFR (class: self-hygiene violation, severity: minor, phase: implement) recorded while building the write-time record-versioning hook.

## Backlog reconciliation note

Audited against the full backlog corpus before creation. The closed record record_versioning_repo_wide_lint built this lint; this defect was found afterward, by the hook task that consumed it, so it is a legitimate recurrence rather than re-litigation of finished work. Open overlaps on reword_dead_lifecycle_command_prose_per_class and contain_deliberate_break_source_mutations are coarse directory-glob footprint matches (scripts/, scripts/tests/), not intent overlap. A serializing dependency edge is carried onto the systematic script-and-test corpus consolidation record, which declares scripts/tests/ and is already planned.

active_projects.title: validate-wiring.sh reports Missing context file for context paths present on disk and in index.json
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/ (never .claude/**, a disposable deploy artifact -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Edit at the path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh.

## Goal

validate-wiring.sh must agree with disk reality: it must not report a context file missing when that file exists at the path it is looking for.

## The defect, as observed

A validate-wiring.sh run emitted 41 FAIL lines, every one reading "Missing context file", for memory, nix and neovim extension context paths. Spot-checked examples: project/memory/learn-usage.md, project/nix/README.md, project/neovim/domain/lua-patterns.md.

Two independent checks contradict the verdict:
- The files PHYSICALLY EXIST at the exact expected path (ls .claude/context/project/memory/learn-usage.md succeeds).
- They are correctly present in .claude/context/index.json with matching path fields.

So this is not a real missing-file condition. It is either a path-resolution defect in the validator (most likely: a prefix, tree-root or relative-vs-absolute mismatch between how index.json records a path and how the validator resolves it) or an environmental quirk in how the validator is invoked.

## Why this is worth fixing

41 FAIL lines that are all false make the validator useless as a gate. Worse, they train a reader to ignore its output, which is how a real missing-context-file regression gets through unnoticed. A validator whose failures are routinely dismissed is a liability rather than a safeguard.

## Required outcome

Root-cause the resolution and make the validator correct. Specifically: determine whether the fault is in the validator or in how it is called, state which, and fix the one that is wrong. If a subset of the 41 turns out to be genuinely missing, separate those from the false positives and report them distinctly rather than collapsing both into one verdict.

## Non-goals

Do not suppress the check or lower its severity to make the output quiet. Silencing a validator that is wrong is strictly worse than leaving it loud, because it removes the signal that something needs attention.

## Acceptance

validate-wiring.sh reports zero "Missing context file" failures for context files that exist on disk and are present in index.json with a matching path, and still fails loudly for a context file genuinely absent from either. A fixture covering both directions is added.

## Provenance

Derived from the orchestration conclusion stage, issue-log entry iss_1793760793964_HkYoUN (class: scope excursion, severity: minor, phase: implement), observed during a deploy-verify step and left unroot-caused as out of that task scope.

## Backlog reconciliation note

Audited against the full backlog corpus before creation. The single mechanically-corroborated open match is reword_dead_lifecycle_command_prose_per_class, whose declared scope is coarse directory globs including scripts/ -- footprint, not intent. No open or closed record addresses this validator defect. The systematic script-and-test corpus consolidation record declares scripts/tests/test-validate-wiring.sh but not validate-wiring.sh itself, so no serializing edge is carried; if the fix turns out to require changes to that test file, add the edge at planning time.

active_projects.title: Allowlist engine-written infrastructure paths in the file_scope Containment sites
active_projects.description:
Admit engine-written infrastructure paths -- starting with specs/events.jsonl -- to the file_scope Containment allowlists, so durable append-only event rows stop being silently dropped from commits.

CITATION: {task 467, iss_1793767328647_oTTy6O}, class "scope excursion": "git-commit-scoped.sh dropped 'specs/events.jsonl' from a commit pathspec: not contained in task #467's declared file_scope."

SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/. Resolve source_dir from <project-root>/.claude-extensions.json and edit at the path mirroring the deployed one. NEVER hand-author under .claude/**, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- an edit there appears to succeed and is silently wiped by the next regeneration (rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). REDEPLOY AFTERWARDS via deploy-headless.sh using the bounded-wait idiom (timeout 540, Bash tool timeout raised to 600000) to RESULT=landed_verify_clean. Never hand-patch a deployed file in place of a redeploy.

CONFIRMED MECHANISM (read directly from the scripts during task creation; do not re-derive from scratch): specs/events.jsonl is a tracked, non-gitignored file (7000+ lines today) that every task's lifecycle appends to via scripts/events-append.sh. It is infrastructure, not task-owned territory, so no task's declared file_scope will ever legitimately contain it. The Containment predicate is checked at THREE independent sites, enumerated in context/standards/git-staging-scope.md's "Three Containment sites, not one." paragraph: (1) orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's WORK (h)/(i) filter, (2) git-commit-phase.sh's Phase-Commit Containment Self-Check, (3) V10 inside git-commit-scoped.sh. Sites 1 and 3 each carry their own hand-copied two-literal allowlist: git-commit-scoped.sh splices ("specs/TODO.md" "specs/state.json") into containment_scope_arr, and WORK (h) splices the same pair into effective_file_scope_json. specs/events.jsonl is in neither.

--- REQUIRED OUTCOMES ---

1. specs/events.jsonl is no longer classified as a file_scope excursion at any of the three Containment sites, and no longer dropped from a commit pathspec that names it.

2. Decide and record whether the allowlist stays a per-site hand-copied literal list or becomes ONE canonical shared definition consumed by every site. This is the third time the same literal pair has been spliced at a sibling site, and the defect recurs once per infrastructure file; the decision determines whether a fourth infrastructure path needs three more edits. Research/plan owns the verdict -- do not assume the answer. Decide at the same time what else belongs on the list (specs/errors.json and other engine-written specs/ state are candidates; an over-wide list would weaken the excursion guard, so justify each member).

3. Determine which caller actually passes specs/events.jsonl in a commit pathspec. A grep of the core scripts during task creation found NO script naming it in a git add / pathspec list, so widening an allowlist alone may fix nothing. orchestrator-postflight.sh:491 and git-commit-phase.sh:197 both build stage_paths as ("${task_dir}/" "specs/TODO.md" "specs/state.json") -- neither stages events.jsonl at all. If the path reaches git-commit-scoped.sh only via a modified_files-derived pathspec, the staging side must be fixed too. Establish the real end-to-end path before asserting a fix works, and verify by observing an actual commit that carries an events.jsonl delta.

4. Record the landing in context/standards/git-staging-scope.md's "Three Containment sites" and "Site 1 carries its own engine-written-state allowlist" paragraphs, so the standard's description of the allowlist stays truthful.

5. Pin the new behavior with fixtures in test-git-commit-scoped.sh and test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, each alongside an assertion that a genuine out-of-scope path is STILL dropped and warned exactly as today -- the drop-and-warn posture must not regress into a blanket pass.

CONCURRENT TERRITORY NOTE: open task #461 (v7_refuses_cached_untracking_pathspec, not_started) also declares git-commit-scoped.sh; #430 and #446 (not_started) declare git-commit-phase.sh and git-staging-scope.md. No dependency edge was added at creation time, but a batch co-scheduling any of these with this task must serialize them rather than run them as parallel siblings.

active_projects.title: Clarify verify-deploy.sh TARGET contract versus its invocation-directory claim
active_projects.description:
Separate verify-deploy.sh's invocation-CWD axis from its TARGET-argument axis, so a reader cannot take "runs correctly from either tree" as permission to pass the source directory as TARGET.

CITATION: {task 468, iss_1793771422937_YOeOmJ}, class "verification tooling note": a plan's Tier Justification named `verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow --only-gate 3,4 <source_dir>` with TARGET=agent-system/extensions/core as the covering check. That errors "no deploy tree", because verify-deploy.sh requires TARGET/.claude to exist and the source directory has no .claude/ subdirectory. The working invocation uses TARGET=the repo root (/home/benjamin/.config/nvim), which holds the deployed .claude/ and is itself the source-store repo; gates 3 and 4 then run and pass.

SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/. Resolve source_dir from <project-root>/.claude-extensions.json and edit at the path mirroring the deployed one. NEVER hand-author under .claude/**, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- an edit there appears to succeed and is silently wiped by the next regeneration (rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). REDEPLOY AFTERWARDS via deploy-headless.sh using the bounded-wait idiom (timeout 540, Bash tool timeout raised to 600000) to RESULT=landed_verify_clean. Never hand-patch a deployed file in place of a redeploy.

CONFIRMED MECHANISM (read directly during task creation): verify-deploy.sh sets TARGET="${TARGET:-$(pwd)}", then CLAUDE_DIR="$TARGET/.claude", and exits 2 with "ERROR: no deploy tree at $CLAUDE_DIR -- nothing to verify." plus "Run: bash deploy-headless.sh $TARGET" when that directory is absent. Separately, every source-store-only gate (3, 4, 6, 7, 12 and others) SKIPs unless $TARGET/agent-system/extensions also exists. The two conditions together mean TARGET must be a repository that simultaneously holds a deployed .claude/ AND the agent-system source store -- i.e. the repo root -- for any source-store gate to actually run rather than SKIP. Nothing in the script states this.

What the header DOES state, in the note landed by completed task #441, is that the script "resolves its TARGET from an explicit argument or `$(pwd)` ... so it runs correctly from either tree with no override". That sentence is true about the INVOCATION DIRECTORY and reads as a claim about the TARGET ARGUMENT. It is the most likely origin of the mistake and must be qualified rather than deleted -- it is correct about its own axis.

--- REQUIRED OUTCOMES ---

1. The header distinguishes the two axes explicitly: where the script may be INVOKED FROM (either tree, no override -- the existing #441 claim) versus what TARGET may BE (a repository containing a deployed .claude/, and additionally containing agent-system/extensions if any source-store-only gate is to run rather than SKIP).

2. The usage line's `[TARGET_REPO]` placeholder carries that contract, including the concrete consequence that `--only-gate 3,4 <source_dir>` cannot work and that the repo root is the correct TARGET for source-store gates.

3. The gate0 error names the convention, not just the missing directory. A reader who passed a source directory should learn from the error text that TARGET must be the repository root holding the deployed tree -- not merely that deploy-headless.sh exists.

4. Decide whether the contract additionally belongs in context/patterns/regeneration-is-manual-only.md's "Root-Resolution Guard for Core Scripts" section, where #441 already documented the adjacent CWD-resolution story and where a planner is plausibly reading, or whether the script header alone suffices. One authority plus pointers, never two partial copies.

5. No behavioral change to any gate's pass/fail semantics. This is a diagnostics-and-documentation task; the only executable change in scope is the gate0 error text.

CONCURRENT TERRITORY NOTE: open tasks #444, #414, #445 and #449 (all not_started) also declare verify-deploy.sh. The sibling task created alongside this one -- the extensions-README-table lint gate -- declares a dependency ON this task, because both edit this file's header and argument-parsing region.
