active_projects.title: Collapse per-path scope excursion issue rows into one record per drop event
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Resolve source_dir from <project-root>/.claude-extensions.json and edit at the path mirroring the deployed one. REDEPLOY AFTERWARDS via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

ORIGIN: Conclusion stage (channel b, agent-system change request) of an /orchestrate invocation, session sess_1793838084_ef69bd. User-approved at the lead level.

=== THE PROBLEM: THE CLASS DESTROYS ITS OWN AGGREGATE SIGNAL ===

123 entries of class "scope excursion" were aggregated from a single /orchestrate invocation -- by far the largest class in the run, more than five times every other class in that aggregate combined. CITATIONS: {task 429, iss_1793840234975_Bu5d3D}, plus 122 entries on task 328 spanning iss_1792181960729_J5c0JK through iss_1793848445269_5W27NH.

At that volume no operator reads the class, and a genuine excursion is indistinguishable from the noise. That is a defect in the RECORDING mechanism, independent of whether any individual drop was correct.

=== MECHANISM, VERIFIED IN THE SOURCE STORE DURING TASK CREATION (re-derive before editing; line numbers move) ===

The class has exactly TWO emitters, and BOTH call issue-record.sh once PER DROPPED PATH from inside a per-path loop:

  1. scripts/git-commit-phase.sh, around line 286, inside `for f in "${files_touched[@]}"` --
     one warn + one issue-record.sh call per uncontained path.
  2. scripts/git-commit-scoped.sh, around line 655, inside the per-pathspec V10 loop --
     same shape, textually distinct message.

Consequence: ONE drop event over a phase that legitimately touched twenty migrated test suites writes TWENTY near-identical issue rows that differ only in the quoted path. The 122 entries on task 328 are not 122 independent incidents; they are a small number of multi-file drop events, fanned out one row per path. A third site, orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's WORK (h)/(i) "EXCURSION DROPPED" filter, prints per-path notices to stderr but does NOT call issue-record.sh -- confirm whether that asymmetry is deliberate before changing it.

=== REQUIRED OUTCOMES ===

1. A single drop event produces a single issue-log record that enumerates the dropped paths, rather than N records each naming one path. Decide the representation (a paths array in the record, a count plus a bounded sample, or grouping at aggregate time) -- research/plan owns the verdict. Do NOT assume the answer, and do NOT suppress information: the full set of dropped paths must remain recoverable from the record, per issue-log.md's no-suppression posture.

2. Decide whether the collapse belongs at the emitter (git-commit-phase.sh and git-commit-scoped.sh each build one record before writing), in issue-record.sh itself (a batch/multi-path call shape), or at read time in issue-grouping.sh / orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh. Note that a read-time-only fix leaves the raw log just as large; an emitter-only fix duplicates the new call shape at two sites. Justify the choice against both.

3. The scope-excursion severity stays `minor` and the posture stays drop-and-warn, never refuse. This task changes how a drop is RECORDED, not whether a drop happens and not what is dropped.

=== EXPLICIT NON-GOALS -- these are owned by existing open tasks, do not re-do or pre-empt them ===

- Whether the containment predicate is too eager, or a task's declared file_scope is too narrow, and the feedback loop that would widen file_scope from observed implement paths: owned by #430 and #446. This task takes NO position on the calibration verdict.
- Allowlisting engine-written or registry infrastructure paths at the three Containment sites: owned by #469, whose own required outcome 2 already asks which further paths belong on the list. One concrete case observed in this run belongs to that task, not this one: the postflight EXCURSION DROPPED path left agent-system/extensions/core/manifest.json uncommitted as an excursion, when registering a newly added script in its extension manifest is the ordinary, expected consequence of adding one. Carry that observation to #469 as evidence; do not fix it here.
- Class-vocabulary normalization and the aggregate's malformed repeated-flag call: owned by #477.

=== SERIALIZATION NOTE ===

file_scope here overlaps #430, #446 and #469 on git-commit-phase.sh, git-commit-scoped.sh and their suites. Those tasks edit the containment PREDICATE and its allowlists; this one edits the RECORDING call beside it. The overlap is real and the work should be serialized behind them rather than run concurrently -- landing the calibration fixes first also shrinks the drop volume this task is measured against.

=== VERIFICATION ===

- test-git-commit-phase.sh and test-git-commit-scoped.sh cover the new record shape: a multi-path drop asserts exactly one issue row naming every dropped path.
- A repo-wide check that no other site emits class "scope excursion" per-path.
- Existing scope-excursion rows in specs/**/issues.jsonl remain parseable by issue-grouping.sh and orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh after the change; a schema change must not strand the existing corpus.

active_projects.title: Recapture corpus baselines under the corrected inventory probe
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET for any agent-system change: agent-system/extensions/core/ (never .claude/**, a disposable deploy artifact -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). This record's primary edit target, however, is this parent record's own plan files under specs/, which are exempt from the no-task-reference and no-record-versioning rules.

GOAL. Recapture the corpus baseline figures that the parent record's net-deletion acceptance criterion is measured against, now that the measurement instrument has been corrected.

=== WHY ===
scripts/script-inventory.sh enumerated the corpus via `git ls-files` alone, so its --size-line and JSON output saw only TRACKED files. A newly created, not-yet-staged file was invisible to the probe. That has now been fixed: the enumeration unions tracked with untracked-but-not-ignored in-corpus files and discloses the contribution via a trailing `untracked=N` field on --size-line plus `untracked_count`/`untracked_paths` in JSON, pinned by a git-fixture regression case.

THE DIRECTION OF THE ERROR IS WHAT MATTERS. An enumeration blind to new untracked files systematically understates insertions, which biases a running insertions-minus-deletions figure in the FAVOURABLE direction -- it makes a phase look more net-negative than it actually was. That is the one direction of error a net-deletion acceptance criterion cannot tolerate, because it hides exactly the drift the criterion exists to catch.

=== WHAT IS AFFECTED (verify before acting; figures drift) ===
Two plan files in the parent record's directory hold baseline figures captured under the old tracked-only behaviour:
  - plans/01_corpus-consolidation-net-deletion.md
  - plans/03_markdown-corpus-consolidation.md
The -10,000 non-test-line floor and the -8,100 markdown target are both stated against those baselines.

The finding was recorded by the record that fixed the probe, which deliberately did NOT edit these files: the parent was an active task at the time and those files were its own territory. Nothing has acted on the finding since. Re-derive which specific figures were captured under the old behaviour rather than assuming all of them were -- some may postdate the fix.

=== SCOPE ===
- Re-run script-inventory.sh against the current tree and record the corrected figures.
- Determine, for each recorded baseline figure in the two plan files above, whether it was captured under the undercounting behaviour. State the finding either way, including for figures that turn out to be unaffected.
- Where a baseline shifts, update it AND restate the running net figure derived from it, so the acceptance criterion is measured against a sound baseline.
- Report the magnitude of the correction explicitly (old figure, new figure, delta). If the correction is immaterial -- the untracked contribution at capture time was zero or negligible -- say so plainly and close; a null result is a valid and useful outcome here, not a failure.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===
- Every baseline figure in the two named plan files is either confirmed sound or corrected, with the determination stated per figure.
- The parent record's running net-deletion figure is restated against the corrected baseline.
- The magnitude of the correction is reported (old, new, delta), including an explicit null result if that is what the measurement shows.

active_projects.title: Stop a required extension manifest.json registration being dropped from a phase commit as a scope excursion
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Edit at the path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

ORIGIN: Conclusion stage (channel b, agent-system changes) of an /orchestrate invocation over task 328, session sess_1793890953_7cb51f. User-approved at the lead level.

SEVERITY: costly. RECURRING -- three separate firings within one task.

CITATIONS -- specs/328_systematic_script_and_test_corpus_efficiency/issues.jsonl:
  iss_1793841635583_gpNhE6 (dispatch_seq 18, Phase 7 -- 47 of 48 migrated test files dropped)
  iss_1793847274112_byw6XR (dispatch_seq 20, Phase 8 -- 51 touched paths dropped)
  iss_1793848518784_26KAZz (dispatch_seq 21, Phase 9 -- 2 paths dropped, one of them manifest.json)

LIVE SYMPTOM: git-commit-phase.sh's Phase-Commit Containment Self-Check drops a legitimately-required manifest.json registration from a phase-closing commit. A phase that extracts a new shared shell library into agent-system/extensions/<ext>/scripts/lib/ must ALSO register that lib in that extension's manifest.json provides.scripts -- scripts/tests/test-manifest-scripts-sync.sh enforces that pairing mechanically. But the containment predicate reads the manifest.json path as a file_scope excursion and drops it, so the phase closes with an incomplete commit and has to pay a separate labeled follow-up commit to recover. Observed in Phase 9 (the install-extension / uninstall-extension pair) and again, identically, in Phase 10 (the typst pair).

WHAT IS ALREADY FIXED -- DO NOT RE-FIX IT (verified in the source store while creating this record; re-derive before editing, line numbers move):
- All three cited entries attribute the drop to a DOUBLE-SLASH glob defect: a trailing-slash file_scope directory entry composing "${entry}/*" into "...tests//*", which never matches a real single-slash child path. THAT DEFECT IS CLOSED. agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/git-commit-phase.sh's is_contained() (around lines 272-305) normalizes a trailing-slash entry down to a bare directory via a `while [ "${entry%/}" != "$entry" ]` loop before composing any glob, and its own comment documents exactly the failure mode those citations describe.
- An engine-written-paths allowlist is also in place: is_contained()'s file_scope array is pre-seeded from lib/engine-written-state-paths-lib.sh, with a hardcoded ("specs/TODO.md", "specs/state.json") pair as the fallback on a source failure.
The citations are therefore retained as the evidence of RECURRENCE and of cost, NOT as a live description of the mechanism. Read them for the cost account, not for the diagnosis.

THE ACTUAL OPEN QUESTION -- a manifest.json registration is a STRUCTURALLY DERIVABLE obligation, not an unforeseeable newly-discovered path. When a phase adds a file under agent-system/extensions/<ext>/scripts/, that extension's own manifest.json registration is required BY A TEST, in the same change. Decide and implement ONE coherent rule, with the reasoning recorded:
(1) Make the containment predicate treat the touched extension's own manifest.json as implicitly in scope whenever the same phase adds or removes a file under that same extension's scripts/ tree. Narrow, mechanically derivable, and prevents the FIRST drop rather than only the repeat. Weigh against: it widens declared territory without review, and file_scope is also the batch admission gate's conflict-detection input and the territory contract between concurrently dispatched tasks.
(2) Surface the obligation as a PRE-COMMIT requirement instead of an implicit widening -- a phase that adds a script under an extension without also touching that extension's manifest.json is told so before the commit fires, leaving the declaration honest and the operator in the loop.
(3) Neither, on the grounding that the general declaration-staleness feedback mechanism (see the territory edges below) subsumes this case once it lands. If this is the ruling, record it explicitly and close this record rather than leaving it open.

NOTE ON THE TASK-LOCAL WORKAROUND: the symptom was worked around for one task alone by widening that task's own declared file_scope (commit 059e41377, which added agent-system/extensions/core/manifest.json and agent-system/extensions/typst/manifest.json to it). That workaround is per-task and does not generalize -- the next task that extracts a lib under a different extension hits the same drop with no declaration covering it. Do not mistake the widened file_scope for a fix.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
- Do NOT weaken the containment predicate for a genuine excursion. Drop-and-warn for an out-of-territory source edit is correct and must survive intact, pinned by a test.
- Do NOT make the check fatal. Fail-open on a missing/empty/malformed file_scope, and never refusing a whole commit over this guard, are both deliberate and must stay.
- Any state.json write must go through the mutex-guarded state-write.sh path, never a second writer.
- Do NOT re-introduce the trailing-slash normalization or the engine-written-paths allowlist; both are already present and must be left working.

VERIFY: extend agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/test-git-commit-phase.sh with fixtures pinning (a) the chosen rule's behaviour for a phase that adds a new script under an extension plus that extension's manifest.json, (b) a genuinely out-of-territory path STILL dropped with its warning and its issue-record.sh call, (c) fail-open behaviour on absent/empty/malformed file_scope unchanged, and (d) the trailing-slash normalization still working.

TERRITORY EDGES -- git-commit-phase.sh is SHARED FILE TERRITORY with three open records, so dependency edges are declared rather than racing them (context/patterns/batch-orchestration-guardrails.md: shared territory is serialized with an edge, never a bare exclusion):
- feed_undeclared_implement_paths_into_file_scope: the general form of this exact problem -- feeding observed-but-undeclared implement paths back into the declaration. If its general mechanism lands first, THIS record may reduce to option (3) above, or to a narrow prevention rule layered on top. Read its description before scoping; it already carries a verified account of git-commit-phase.sh's drop site and of the proposed_file_scope channel.
- close_the_plan_to_file_scope_reconciliation_gap: owns the plan-to-file_scope harvest path (plan-file-scope-harvest.sh, skill-base.sh) and makes a containment drop non-advisory. A manifest.json registration is exactly the kind of path a plan's "Files to modify" block may or may not name, so the two interact directly.
- collapse_perpath_scope_excursion_issue_rows_into_one: rewrites the per-path issue-record.sh emission inside the very loop this record changes.

active_projects.title: Stop the identical-dispatch convergence guard halting a task whose previous cycle closed a phase
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Edit at the path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

ORIGIN: Conclusion stage (channel b, agent-system changes) of an /orchestrate invocation over task 328, session sess_1793890953_7cb51f. User-approved at the lead level.

SEVERITY: costly. OBSERVED FIRST-HAND. There is NO issues.jsonl citation for this record -- the orchestrate lead's own observation during the originating run, recorded verbatim below, IS the evidence. Do not go looking for a citation that does not exist.

LIVE SYMPTOM: the identical-dispatch convergence guard halts a task on cycle 2 even when cycle 1 closed a real plan phase, capping every /orchestrate invocation at exactly one phase of progress.

EVIDENCE (session sess_1793890953_7cb51f, task 328):
- Cycle 1 dispatched general-implementation-agent for task 328 at dispatch_seq 22. It closed Phase 10 of specs/328_systematic_script_and_test_corpus_efficiency/plans/03_markdown-corpus-consolidation.md, advancing that plan 9/20 -> 10/20 phases, committed as 7a47a6a57 and f41aecf54.
- Cycle 2's orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh then composed dispatch 24, found its content byte-identical to dispatch 22's, reported `IDENTICAL DISPATCH ... (streak=2)`, and issued `IDENTICAL DISPATCH HALT: task #328 ... halting this task for the rest of the run`.
- The guard's own stated premise -- that re-issuing an identical dispatch means no progress is being made -- was therefore FALSE here: progress was made AND committed between the two compositions.

ROOT CAUSE, VERIFIED IN THE SOURCE STORE (re-derive before editing; line numbers move):
- The composed dispatch body's ONLY phase-progress interpolation is the `PHASES COMPLETED: <n> of <m>` line inside orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh's `## Phase Mission` section (around line 617), and that entire section is gated on `[ -n "$phase_number" ]` (around line 604).
- `--phase-number` is set by orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh at ONE site only (around line 2633): `[ -n "${h1_next_phase[$t]:-}" ] && build_args+=(--phase-number "${h1_next_phase[$t]}")`, whose own comment states it is "only ever set for a hard-mode implement candidate".
- Therefore an ordinary (non-hard-mode) implement dispatch carries NO phase-progress content whatsoever. Two consecutive cycles for the same task, phase and plan hash identically no matter how many phases landed in between.
- cycle_plan_dispatch_hash() (orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, around line 2160 onward) strips exactly three per-cycle-varying lines before hashing: `- dispatch_seq: N`, `- dispatch_start_ts: N`, and the Issue Log's `--what-happened "..." [--phase P] [--dispatch-seq N] \` boilerplate line. Its own header comment asserts that "a real behavioral change to the dispatch (a different phase_number, a different territory payload, a different focus string) changes some OTHER line and therefore still changes the digest". For a non-hard-mode implement dispatch that assertion does not hold: closing a phase changes no line of the body. Correcting that comment is part of this work, not an afterthought.

SCOPE -- decide and implement, with the reasoning recorded. The three candidate directions below are the originating lead's own framing and are NOT a prescription; they are not mutually exclusive:
(a) Include phase progress in the dispatch content the guard hashes -- emit the completed-phase count, or the next-unstarted-phase identity, into the dispatch body for every implement dispatch rather than only a hard-mode one. Note the STANDING OBLIGATION recorded in cycle_plan_dispatch_hash()'s own header: any new per-cycle-varying content added to a composed dispatch file MUST be reconciled with the strip pattern in the SAME change, or the halt silently goes inert. Phase progress is per-PROGRESS-varying, not per-cycle-varying, so it must NOT be stripped -- state that distinction explicitly wherever it is added, as the existing DECIDED AND RECORDED rulings in that header do.
(b) Have the guard consult an independent progress signal before halting -- the committed phase count, or `phases_completed` from the handoff file, which orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh already reads (around lines 322-331). A streak would then be charged only when the hash matches AND no phase advanced. Compare with the deploy_pending streak-FREEZE backstop immediately above the halt block: that is the established in-codebase precedent for "do not charge churn when an independent signal explains the repetition", and it freezes rather than suppresses, so a pre-existing genuine streak survives the interruption intact.
(c) Both.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
- The guard MUST still fire for genuine non-convergence. A task that truly re-issues the same dispatch with nothing landing must still halt; this record must not neuter the guard.
- Preserve the deploy_pending streak-freeze semantics and the hash-degradation posture (sha256sum unavailable, or the just-written dispatch file unreadable, leaves the streak at 0 and disables the guard for the run with a named stderr notice -- never fatal, never a silent skip).
- Preserve the two DECIDED AND RECORDED non-strip rulings in cycle_plan_dispatch_hash()'s header (the `## Batch Gate Deferral` and `## Outstanding Gate Finding` sections stay unstripped), or restate them with fresh justification if the chosen mechanism genuinely requires revisiting them.
- The halt's existing clean back-out must survive intact: pre-dispatch status restore via state-write.sh, task-lock release, and no budget charge, no --flush-seq, no pending_dispatch record, no dispatch row for the halted task.

VERIFY: a regression test MUST pin that a cycle which closed a phase is NOT halted by this guard, and a companion fixture MUST pin that a cycle which closed nothing still IS halted. Site both alongside the existing coverage in agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, whose "Group 27" fixtures already own this guard -- its Case F pins the strip-pattern-drift failure mode that once left the halt inert, and is the model to follow.

COST OF LEAVING IT: every /orchestrate N over a multi-phase plan yields at most one phase of progress. The plan cited above alone has 10 phases remaining -- ten separate invocations instead of progress within one run.

TERRITORY EDGES -- orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh and orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh are SHARED FILE TERRITORY with several open records, so an edge is declared rather than racing them (context/patterns/batch-orchestration-guardrails.md):
- hoist_batch_gate_deferral_directive: its option (1) re-emits `## Batch Gate Deferral` at a different position in the SAME composed dispatch body this record adds content to, and the hash normalizer carries an explicit DECIDED AND RECORDED ruling about that very section. Dependency edge declared: these two must be ordered, not raced.
- Also writing one or both of these two scripts; no ordering declared here, but re-check at admission: warn_plan_size_exceeds_cycle_budget, validate_settled_route_before_dispatch, advise_on_dirty_file_scope_at_admission, validate_carried_unverified_names_a_source, snapshot_lean_challenge_at_plan_time.

active_projects.title: Adjudicate where MCP write-tool permission grants belong: repo-scoped extension fragment vs. the server owner's own configuration
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Resolve source_dir from <project-root>/.claude-extensions.json and edit at the path mirroring the deployed one. REDEPLOY AFTERWARDS via deploy-headless.sh using the bounded-wait idiom (timeout 540, Bash tool timeout 600000). Re-derive every quoted clause from the source store, never from a deployed copy. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** .

FINDING (recorded during the sapience extension build, issues.jsonl class scope-mismatch, severity minor): the sapience extension's settings-fragment.json grants four MCP write tools (sapience_remember, sapience_wrapup, sapience_handoff, sapience_adddoc) at THIS repository's project scope. That closes the autonomous-dispatch permission blocker inside this repo and is correct for that purpose. But context/standards/mcp-server-ownership.md's own rule states that permission grants for a given MCP server belong with the entity that OWNS the server registration -- here ~/.dotfiles/config/claude/settings.json, whose keys are reset from the dotfiles repo by home.activation.claudeSettings on every home-manager switch. The two placements are in tension and the tension is currently unresolved rather than decided.

Note the enforcement asymmetry that makes this non-obvious: the dotfiles copy is machine-wide and nix-enforced (so an extension CANNOT durably write it -- an edit there would be reverted on the next switch), while the repo-scoped fragment is the only placement an extension can actually own. A verdict of 'the repo-scoped fragment is correct' is therefore legitimate; it just has to be STATED rather than left as an apparent standards violation.

DECIDE, do not assume: (a) whether mcp-server-ownership.md's rule should be amended to carve out the nix-enforced-settings case explicitly, or whether the sapience grant should move to ~/.dotfiles and the extension stop granting it; (b) whether a repo-scoped write-tool grant for a server the repo does not own needs any additional operator-visible disclosure. Reason about the security posture of the narrower-scope placement on its own merits, not only about which file the standard currently names.

ACCEPTANCE: mcp-server-ownership.md states a verdict covering the nix-enforced-settings case; the sapience extension's grant placement matches that verdict; verify-deploy.sh gate set green after redeploy.

artifacts.summary: Verdict: sapience extension's project-scoped grant of its four MCP write tools is a legitimate, deliberate narrower-than-registration-scope exception (bounds unreviewed personal-vault writes to one repo), not a standards violation; recommends amending mcp-server-ownership.md with an explicit carve-out naming this pattern rather than moving the grant to ~/.dotfiles.
3-phase plan: standard carve-out amendment + symmetric disclosure links + redeploy and full gate verification.

active_projects.title: Derive gate-count expectations in sibling test suites from the live gate registry
active_projects.description:
Make the gate-count expectations in two sibling test suites derive from the live gate registry instead of hardcoding integers, so that registering a new gate requires no edits to unrelated suites.

CHANNEL: /orchestrate conclusion channel (c), follow-up task, session sess_1793897002_11e720.
CITATION: {task 471, iss_1793898478763_2WjvRL}, class "test-fixture-drift".

THE PROBLEM, VERIFIED: registering gate 26 broke five hardcoded assertions across two suites that are not about the new gate at all:
  scripts/tests/test-gate-registry-resolution.sh -- case1 expected exactly 25 ids; case32 and case33 hardcoded 25 as the live max and 26 as one-past-max.
  scripts/tests/test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh -- case (c) used 24 as an out-of-range probe id; case (d) iterated `seq 1 23`.
All five were mechanically bumped to the new live max (26) and one-past (27) to land that work. That fix-up is correct but not durable: the next gate registered repeats it exactly, and because neither suite is in a gate-adding task's natural file_scope, it also repeats the declared-scope widening that was needed to commit it.

WHY IT MATTERS: verify-deploy.sh already dispatches gates dynamically via gate_registry_ids plus "gate${id}_run", so adding a gate needs only a gate-registry.data row and a gateN_run function -- no call-site list. These two test suites are the sole remaining place where a hardcoded gate count survives, which makes them a recurring, avoidable tax on every future gate and a standing source of spurious red.

--- REQUIRED OUTCOMES ---

1. Derive the live max gate id and the one-past-max probe id from gate_registry_ids (the same source verify-deploy.sh's own --only-gate bound already derives from) rather than writing integers into assertions. Do not merely move the integers into a variable initialised to a literal -- the value must come from the registry at test time.

2. Preserve each assertion's intent. Case (c)'s out-of-range probe must still probe genuinely out-of-range, and case (d)'s enumeration must still cover exactly the real id set. A derived value that silently makes an assertion vacuous is a regression, not a fix: show for each converted assertion that it still fails when it should.

3. Add a guard that the suites' own notion of the id set matches verify-deploy.sh's, so the two cannot drift apart in the other direction.

4. Verify by registering a throwaway gate in a fixture (never in the real gate-registry.data) and confirming both suites stay green without edits.

CONCURRENT TERRITORY NOTE: the creation-time proposal audit returned three mechanically-corroborated
subset-of-open verdicts, each sharing BOTH of this task's declared paths: record 328
(systematic_script_and_test_corpus_efficiency, which declares the whole scripts/tests/ directory),
record 435 (reword_dead_lifecycle_command_prose_per_class) and record 448
(contain_deliberate_break_source_mutations). Records 418 and 414 additionally declare
scripts/gate-registry.data. Serialize against all of these rather than co-scheduling in parallel;
the audit passed both its mechanical and semantic gates, so these are ordering constraints, not a
duplication verdict.

active_projects.title: Make generate-task-order.sh read active_goal so the field stops being a dead write
active_projects.description:
Make generate-task-order.sh read `active_goal` from state.json so the field stops being a dead write: it is declared, documented, validated, and written, but no consumer ever reads it.

THE GAP, VERIFIED (2026-11-05):
- Declared: context/schemas/state-schema.json:164 defines `active_goal`.
- Documented: context/reference/state-management-schema.md:77 describes it as a free-prose statement of the repository's current goal.
- Validated: scripts/validate-state.sh:858 lists `active_goal` among recognized widened fields, so writing it passes validation cleanly.
- Written: commands/review.md:734-740 (Section 6.7.3) writes `.active_goal` via `state-write.sh ... --regen-todo`, explicitly so the TODO.md regeneration happens inside the same mutex as the write that triggered it.
- NEVER READ: scripts/generate-task-order.sh resolves the Goal line only from (a) an explicit `--goal TEXT` override (GOAL_OVERRIDE, lines ~92, 110-112, 1040-1042) or (b) read_existing_goal() (lines ~909-931), which greps the existing `**Goal**: ` line back out of TODO.md. `grep -n active_goal scripts/generate-task-order.sh` returns nothing.

REPRODUCED: in a consumer repo, writing active_goal via `state-write.sh ... --regen-todo` succeeded (state.json updated) but TODO.md was left byte-identical with no Goal line, because TODO.md had no prior Goal line for read_existing_goal() to recover. The line rendered only after manually passing `--goal "$(jq -r .active_goal specs/state.json)"` to `generate-task-order.sh --update-todo`. Any caller that sets active_goal expecting it to render hits the same silent no-op; /review Section 6.7.3 is the one in-tree caller that does.

--- REQUIRED OUTCOMES ---

1. generate-task-order.sh resolves the Goal line from a defined precedence: explicit `--goal` override first, then state.json `active_goal`, then the existing TODO.md Goal line (current read_existing_goal behavior), then omit the line entirely. The existing `--goal` and preserve-across-regeneration behaviors must not regress.

2. Decide and record the conflict rule between a state.json `active_goal` and a hand-edited TODO.md Goal line. The preserve-from-TODO behavior exists so regeneration does not clobber a human edit; giving active_goal higher precedence means a stale active_goal silently overwrites hand edits. State the chosen rule and its rationale rather than leaving it implicit in the code.

3. context/formats/task-order-format.md documents the full precedence. Its Goal Statement section currently documents only the preserve-from-TODO and `--goal` behaviors; the Generation and Generation Algorithm sections, which enumerate what the script reads, also need the new source listed.

4. A regression case in scripts/tests/test-generate-task-order.sh: with `active_goal` set in state.json and no Goal line present in TODO.md, `--update-todo` must emit the Goal line. That is the exact condition which silently no-ops today, so the test must fail against the current script.

5. Confirm whether commands/review.md Section 6.7.3 needs any change once the reader exists. Its `--regen-todo` rationale becomes accurate rather than aspirational, so a comment or no change may suffice. Do not widen scope to other callers unless they are found to write active_goal.

active_projects.title: Fix the Pass-2 semantic scorer whose normalization inflates against verbose corpus records
active_projects.description:
Fix the Pass-2 semantic scorer in audit-task-proposals.sh, whose normalization inflates scores against verbose corpus records and so fires duplicate-of-open on proposals that share only house boilerplate.

THE DEFECT, VERIFIED (2026-11-05, measured with the script's own tokenizer):
`token_overlap_score($ta; $tb)` (scripts/audit-task-proposals.sh, in JQ_PROGRAM_BODY) computes `$inter / ([$la, $lb] | min)` -- the overlap coefficient normalized by the SMALLER token set. Because corpus records in this repo carry long, structured descriptions, the smaller side is almost always the incoming proposal, so the score becomes "what fraction of MY tokens appear anywhere in that record". A verbose record therefore matches nearly every proposal.

Measured on one real pair (proposal "make generate-task-order.sh read active_goal" vs record 390 migrate_mis_sited_agent_system_tasks):
  proposal unique tokens: 195
  record unique tokens:   933
  shared tokens:          110
  score as implemented (/ min):  0.564  -- clears SEMANTIC_THRESHOLD 0.4, emits duplicate-of-open
  Jaccard (/ union):             0.108  -- far below 0.4
The 110 shared tokens are house style, not subject matter: agent-system, extensions, core, scripts, state, json, specs, write, and similar. The two tasks have no subject overlap and no shared file_scope.

OBSERVED BLAST RADIUS: that proposal drew 56 non-genuinely-new, non-scope-blind verdicts, every one with `shared_paths: null` and `mechanical_class: "none"` (i.e. zero mechanical corroboration). Top semantic matches included consent_gated_git_push (0.63) and guard_latex_builds_against_vimtex_watcher (0.574), neither related to a Goal-line reader. The proposal was in fact genuinely new.

CONSTRAINT FROM THE EXISTING DESIGN: the SEMANTIC_THRESHOLD comment block states the constant is deliberately lenient per the False-Negative Posture in context/patterns/backlog-reconciliation.md, and that it must be tuned "ONLY after re-measuring both error costs, never to quiet down a noisy run". This task must therefore change the METRIC and re-measure, not merely lower the constant. The recall-biased posture itself is sound and should be preserved: a missed near-duplicate is the expensive error.

--- REQUIRED OUTCOMES ---

1. Replace or correct the normalization so score no longer depends on corpus-record verbosity. Evaluate at least Jaccard (intersection over union) and proposal-side normalization, and state why the chosen metric is right. The asymmetry, not the constant, is the defect.

2. Reduce boilerplate inflation. The current stopword list covers English function words but none of this repo's structural vocabulary. Consider document-frequency weighting across the corpus, or stripping structural scaffolding (section banners such as the REQUIRED OUTCOMES header, path fragments, fenced blocks) before tokenizing. Do not hand-extend the stopword list with repo nouns as the whole fix -- that does not generalize to other deploys.

3. Re-measure SEMANTIC_THRESHOLD against the new metric and record both error costs, per the existing comment block's own instruction. Update the comment block and the False-Negative Posture section of context/patterns/backlog-reconciliation.md (section at :104) so the stated rationale matches the implemented metric.

4. Regression coverage in scripts/tests/test-audit-task-proposals.sh: a proposal paired with a long, unrelated corpus record that shares only structural vocabulary must NOT clear the threshold. Build the fixture from the measured pair above so the test fails against the current scorer.

5. Preserve the mechanically-corroborated path exactly. Verdicts backed by a real file-footprint class (exact/subset/superset/overlap) must keep firing regardless of semantic score; only Pass-2-only verdicts are in scope for this change.

OUT OF SCOPE (deliberately, decided at creation):

1. The consumer-side confirm contract -- the label-only verdict filter in commands/task.md, commands/review.md and commands/errors.md, which prompts on any non-genuinely-new verdict regardless of corroboration. Now filed as its own task (492), which depends on THIS task and carries a precondition to re-measure against the corrected scorer before implementing. If the scorer fix here drops verdict volume enough that the prompt stops misfiring, that task shrinks to a documentation change.

2. The size of the audit_verdict blob persisted into state.json -- one task entry added roughly 970 lines / 97 verdict rows under the current scorer. Still unfiled on purpose: it is downstream of this fix, so measure the post-fix blob before deciding what is worth persisting, and file it then if it still warrants a task.

SOURCE STORE: all edits land in agent-system/extensions/core/ in this repo, never in a deployed .claude/** tree -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md.

active_projects.title: Make backlog-audit corroboration computable and gate the confirm prompt on it
active_projects.description:
Key the backlog-audit confirmation prompt to corroboration rather than to the verdict label, and define that bar once instead of re-deriving it at each consumer.

--- PRECONDITION: RE-MEASURE BEFORE IMPLEMENTING ---

This task was filed from evidence gathered against the PRE-FIX scorer. Before implementing anything, re-run audit-task-proposals.sh against the corrected scorer and record the new numbers. If the corrected scorer alone drops the verdict volume to the point where the prompt no longer misfires on genuinely-new proposals, then outcomes 2 and 3 below shrink to a documentation change (state the bar explicitly) and the consumer edits may be unnecessary. Do NOT implement the full change on the strength of the measurements quoted here. The dependency on the scorer task exists for exactly this reason. Outcome 1 is exempt from this precondition: it is a wiring defect, not a calibration question.

THE DEFECT, INDEPENDENT OF SCORER CALIBRATION:
Each consumer filters the audit's verdict set by LABEL alone -- it drops `genuinely-new` and `scope-blind` and prompts if anything at all remains:
  commands/task.md:181    backlog_verdicts=$(... select(.verdict != "genuinely-new" and .verdict != "scope-blind") ...)
  commands/review.md:519  the same jq predicate, verbatim
  commands/errors.md:145  the same rule stated as prose
Nothing in any of the three keys on whether the verdict carries mechanical corroboration. That contradicts the script's own contract: the audit-task-proposals.sh header states Pass 2 is "a recall-biased, over-inclusive SHORTLIST" and that a verdict emitted purely from Pass 2 with no mechanical corroboration "is not a certified fact". The consumers nonetheless treat such a verdict as prompt-worthy, which is a design mismatch that a better-calibrated scorer does not by itself repair.

It also contradicts the consumers' own stated intent. Each site carries the instruction that when the filtered set is empty the prompt must be skipped entirely, because the check "must never add friction to the common genuinely-new case". With a label-only filter over a deliberately lenient threshold, the filtered set is almost never empty, so the escape hatch never fires.

OBSERVED (pre-fix scorer, 2026-11-05): two proposals that were in fact genuinely new drew 56 and 20 non-genuinely-new, non-scope-blind verdicts respectively. Every one had `shared_paths: null` and `mechanical_class: "none"` -- zero mechanical corroboration. Both prompts were overridden on inspection. A gate that is correct to override on essentially every firing trains the override rather than the check.

COMPANION DEFECT, AND THE REASON THE FILTER FIRES ON EVERYTHING: Pass 1 never runs at any call site.
audit-task-proposals.sh accepts `--file-scope JSON_ARRAY` (usage at :94, :130; parsed at :158), and the mechanical file-footprint comparison is the pass the design treats as authoritative corroboration. NO CALLER PASSES IT. Every invocation sends only --title/--description/--id:
  commands/review.md:517
  commands/task.md:179
  commands/errors.md
  skills/skill-fix-it/SKILL.md
  skills/skill-spawn/SKILL.md
  context/workflows/meta-interview.md (two invocations)
With no proposal file_scope supplied, the mechanical pass has nothing to compare, so it can only ever return `mechanical_class: "none"` and `shared_paths: null`. Every verdict the system produces is therefore semantic-only BY CONSTRUCTION, which is also exactly why a corroboration-based filter would currently filter nothing: corroboration is never computed.

Demonstrated: an audit run for a proposal to fix the --depends-on-add not_started gap reported zero corroborated verdicts, even though task 500 (edge_backfill_unreachable_for_not_started) declares precisely scripts/update-task-status.sh and scripts/tests/test-update-task-status.sh -- a dead-on footprint match that Pass 1 would have caught had it been given the proposal's scope. The duplicate was found only by a manual file_scope query. This is the near-duplicate-with-shared-paths failure the script exists to catch, missed because its authoritative pass was never fed.

NOT IN SCOPE: the hook hooks/validate-task-creation-audit.sh is correct as written and must not change. It enforces only that a task-creating state write RECORDED an audit (--audit-verdict / --audit-override), and deliberately does not parse verdicts. The prompting decision is the command layer's, which is where this task operates.

--- REQUIRED OUTCOMES ---

1. Pass the proposal's file_scope to the audit at EVERY call site listed above, so the mechanical pass can actually run. This is a prerequisite for outcomes 2 and 3: a corroboration-based bar is meaningless while corroboration is structurally uncomputable. This outcome is NOT contingent on the re-measurement precondition -- it is a wiring defect that holds regardless of how the semantic scorer is calibrated, and it should be fixed even if every other outcome here is dropped. Where a call site does not yet know the proposal's paths, decide whether to derive them or to record explicitly that the call is semantic-only.

2. Define the prompt-worthiness bar once, in context/patterns/backlog-reconciliation.md, as a named rule the consumers reference. The bar must distinguish a mechanically corroborated verdict (mechanical_class exact/subset/superset/overlap, or non-null shared_paths) from a Pass-2-only verdict, consistent with the script header's own statement about what each is worth. Decide and record whether a Pass-2-only verdict should prompt at a higher semantic bar, be reported without prompting, or be summarized as a count.

3. Have commands/task.md, commands/review.md, and commands/errors.md reference that single rule instead of each carrying its own copy of the predicate. This mirrors the consolidation already done for topic assignment, where context/patterns/topic-assignment-pattern.md replaced several inline copies; the same duplication is re-forming here across three sites.

4. Preserve the corroborated path's behavior exactly. A verdict with a real file-footprint class must still prompt, and `covered-by-closed` must still name the discharging artifact's path rather than a bare archived task number.

5. Keep the recall-biased posture intact. The point is to change what the CONSUMER does with an over-inclusive shortlist, not to narrow what the audit detects. Do not raise SEMANTIC_THRESHOLD as part of this task; that constant belongs to the scorer task.

6. Reconcile docs/reference/standards/multi-task-creation-standard.md if it restates the label-only filter, so the standard and the pattern doc agree.

STILL UNFILED, deliberately: the size of the audit_verdict blob persisted into state.json (one task's entry added roughly 970 lines / 97 verdict rows pre-fix). It is downstream of the scorer fix in the same way this task is -- measure the post-fix blob before deciding what is worth persisting, and file it then if it still warrants a task.

SOURCE STORE: all edits land in agent-system/extensions/core/ in this repo, never in a deployed .claude/** tree -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md.

active_projects.title: Fix plan-format.md Tier Justification: a suite entry point that cannot resolve and a selector result asserted instead of measured
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Resolve the extension's own source_dir from <project-root>/.claude-extensions.json and edit at the path mirroring the deployed one; note that file carries NO top-level source_dir, only per-extension entries. REDEPLOY AFTERWARDS via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

ORIGIN: conclusion stage (channel b, agent-system changes) of an /orchestrate invocation over task 878 in ~/Projects/BimodalLogic, session sess_1793904111_6edc04. User-approved at the lead level.

SEVERITY: minor (both defects).

TWO DEFECTS, ONE FILE, ONE SUBSECTION -- filed together deliberately. Both land in the `**Tier Justification**:` block of agent-system/extensions/core/context/formats/plan-format.md (around lines 332-345). Shared file territory is a reason to batch, never to separate.

CITATIONS -- ~/Projects/BimodalLogic/specs/878_lplus_ztime_decidability_paper_proof_repair/issues.jsonl (that repository, NOT this one):
  iss_1793905878455_9R7xHR -- defect 1
  iss_1793905661566_XjC7uq -- defect 2

=== DEFECT 1: a suite entry point that cannot resolve in a deploy-target repository ===

MEASURED. plan-format.md line 339 names the suite-subset narrowing mechanism as, verbatim:

    bash agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/run-all.sh --only SUITE[,SUITE,...]

In a deploy-target repository there is no agent-system/ directory at all (verified: ~/Projects/BimodalLogic has none), so a plan author following that line verbatim is handed a nonexistent path. The working entry point there is `bash .claude/scripts/tests/run-all.sh --only ...`. The line is inconsistent even within its own list: the sibling bullet two lines below already uses the deploy form, `bash .claude/scripts/verify-deploy.sh --only-gate N[,M,...]`.

THE DOCUMENT ALREADY STATES THE CORRECT RULE, 80 LINES LATER -- do not invent a new convention. The same file's forcing-override section (around lines 420-429) sets out the dual-form convention explicitly: the deploy form `bash .claude/scripts/tests/run-all.sh --only SUITE[,SUITE...]` "in a deploy-target repository", or "the parallel `bash agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/run-all.sh --only SUITE[,SUITE...]` ... form when the dispatch is composed from inside the agent-system source-store repository itself", and then: "The composer resolves and interpolates whichever of the two actually exists in the repository the dispatch is running in (never a hardcoded path that cannot resolve there); if neither exists, the directive degrades to stating the full gate set as such instead of naming a dead path." Line 339 violates a rule its own document already owns. Apply that rule at line 339 BY REFERENCE -- do not fork a second verbatim copy of the convention; a duplicated contract is how the two statements drifted apart in the first place.

=== DEFECT 2: a Tier Justification line asserted a selector result instead of measuring it ===

A prior plan for task 878 asserted, in two separate Tier Justification lines, that specs/ROADMAP.md resolves to the `__FULL_SWEEP__` sentinel under `suite_selection_select` -- i.e. that no suite covers it.

MEASURED directly this run, from the deploy tree:

    suite_selection_select specs/ROADMAP.md
    -> test-engine-written-state-paths-lib.sh test-roadmap-generation.sh

Two covering suites, not the sentinel. Only a different path in that same plan (a report path) actually returns `__FULL_SWEEP__`. So a Tier Justification line carried a false claim about the selector's own output, and nothing in the standard required the author to run the selector before writing the claim.

THE PATTERN, not the single wrong line, is the subject: a Tier Justification is the one sentence that licenses a phase to verify below `full`. An unmeasured claim there can silently under-verify a phase.

=== SCOPE -- decide and implement ONE coherent rule per defect, recording the reasoning ===

(1) ENTRY POINT. Make line 339 name a form that resolves in both repository shapes, governed by the resolve-whichever-exists rule the override section already states, referenced rather than restated.

(2) MEASUREMENT. Decide whether plan-format.md's Tier Justification requirement should REQUIRE the author to have run `suite_selection_select` on the touched path(s) and quote its actual output in the line, rather than asserting a covering suite or the `__FULL_SWEEP__` sentinel. Weigh honestly: a measurement requirement makes every non-final sub-`full` phase pay a selector invocation at plan time, and plan-format.md is already a long standard whose requirements compete for an author's attention; against that, an unmeasured tier claim can license under-verification of a phase, which is the whole point of the field. Consider explicitly whether a MECHANICAL check -- a plan lint that re-runs the selector for any Tier Justification naming a suite subset or the sentinel, and fails on a mismatch -- is the sounder enforcement than a prose requirement that relies on instruction-following. State the ruling either way; do not leave it implicit.

=== HARD CONSTRAINTS ===
- Do NOT change the tier taxonomy, the final-phase `full` invariant, or the rule that the final phase carries no justification line.
- Do NOT weaken or remove the `__FULL_SWEEP__` documentation around line 342; it is correct and is what made defect 2 diagnosable.
- Keep the override section's dual-form convention as the SINGLE statement of that rule. Reference it; do not copy it.
- If remedy (2) selects a lint, file_scope must be widened at plan time to cover the lint script, its test suite, and any gate wiring -- this record declares only plan-format.md.

=== TERRITORY NOTE ===
The creation-time backlog audit returned mechanical `subset-of-open` overlap on agent-system/extensions/core/context/formats/plan-format.md against open tasks 459, 328, 360, 385 and 420. None of them addresses either defect above. If any is dispatched concurrently with this one, the shared file must be sequenced, not run in parallel.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===
- Line 339 names a form that resolves in a deploy-target repository AND in the source-store repository, under the convention the override section already states.
- A grep of plan-format.md for the bare `agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/run-all.sh` path returns only occurrences explicitly paired with the deploy form or explicitly labelled as the source-store-repository form.
- The measurement ruling is recorded with its reasoning, including why a lint was or was not added.
- If a lint is added, a fixture proves a Tier Justification carrying a fabricated selector result fails, and one carrying the measured result passes.

active_projects.title: Exempt a task own artifact directory from the phase-commit containment predicate
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Resolve the extension's own source_dir from <project-root>/.claude-extensions.json and edit at the path mirroring the deployed one; note that file carries NO top-level source_dir, only per-extension entries. REDEPLOY AFTERWARDS via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

ORIGIN: conclusion stage (channel b, agent-system changes) of an /orchestrate invocation over task 878 in ~/Projects/BimodalLogic, session sess_1793904111_6edc04. User-approved at the lead level.

SEVERITY: minor as recorded, but the effect is a task's OWN required artifact silently omitted from its OWN phase commit.

CITATION -- ~/Projects/BimodalLogic/specs/878_lplus_ztime_decidability_paper_proof_repair/issues.jsonl (that repository, NOT this one): iss_1793906925617_Kqxs0T

LIVE SYMPTOM: git-commit-phase.sh dropped

    specs/878_lplus_ztime_decidability_paper_proof_repair/reports/01_lplus-ztime-decidability-proof-repair.md

from a phase commit pathspec, warning that it was "not contained in this task's declared file_scope". The dropped path is that task's own research report, sitting under that task's own artifact directory. A task's own artifact directory should never need an explicit file_scope declaration to be committable by that same task's own phase commit.

=== MECHANICS VERIFIED IN THE SOURCE STORE (re-derive before editing; line numbers move) ===

The defect is an ASYMMETRY BETWEEN TWO DIFFERENT CONSTRUCTS INSIDE THE SAME SCRIPT, agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/git-commit-phase.sh:

- `stage_paths` (around line 201) is seeded ("${task_dir}/" "specs/TODO.md" "specs/state.json"). The task's own directory IS staged unconditionally and sits structurally outside the self-check.
- `file_scope_arr` -- the array the `is_contained()` containment predicate tests each `files_touched` entry against (around lines 237-270) -- is widened with the engine-written-state paths read from scripts/lib/engine-written-state-paths-lib.sh, plus a literal ("specs/TODO.md", "specs/state.json") fallback pair. It is NOT widened with `task_dir`.

So a `files_touched` entry under the task's own directory is staged by the seed and then flagged and REMOVED from the pathspec by the self-check. The script's own comment around lines 197-199 already warns that the two are a "DIFFERENT construct"; the member missing from the second one is the task's own directory.

=== WHY THIS IS A PROPAGATION GAP, NOT A NEW IDEA ===

agent-system/extensions/core/context/standards/git-staging-scope.md's "Three Containment sites, not one" section names three independent sites checking the SAME containment predicate. The own-task-directory exemption already exists at two of them:

- Site 1, orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's WORK (h) advisory, gained the dispatching task's own resolved directory as an implicit, unconditional in-scope member under completed project 284. That record's stated reason for making the exemption WHOLE-DIRECTORY was explicit parity with "the commit pipeline, which already stages the whole directory regardless of declared scope."
- Site 3, git-commit-scoped.sh's V10 gate, splices the contending task's own directory into `containment_scope_arr` (around lines 491-496), with a comment noting the carve-out "lives under the task's own directory, which this implicit member already" covers.
- Site 2, git-commit-phase.sh's Phase-Commit Containment Self-Check, never received it.

The observed drop is precisely that gap. Note the irony to be recorded: project 284's parity assumption -- that the commit pipeline already covers the whole task directory regardless of declared scope -- is TRUE of git-commit-phase.sh's staging seed and FALSE of its containment self-check, which is exactly the distinction this defect exposes.

A sibling precedent for the shape of the fix: completed project 425 added the (specs/TODO.md, specs/state.json) literal pair to site 1's effective scope, explicitly "mirroring the existing V10 allowlist already landed in git-commit-scoped.sh at a sibling, non-subsuming containment site," and recorded the relationship in git-staging-scope.md. Follow that shape.

=== ESTABLISH THIS BEFORE EDITING ===

This run's pre-dispatch review separately flagged task 878 as `file_scope is missing_key` and admitted it carrying an `absent_scope_advisory`. But the predicate FAILS OPEN on a missing, empty, unreadable or malformed file_scope -- a genuinely absent key should have skipped the containment check entirely and dropped nothing. Determine why a drop fired anyway for a task reported as missing the key. Candidates to test, not to assume: the key was present-but-not-covering by the time the phase commit ran (e.g. populated between review and commit by an earlier postflight's --file-scope-add union merge); or the review and the commit read different state; or the fail-open guard does not cover the observed shape of "missing". This decides whether the fix is only the missing task_dir member or ALSO a fail-open defect, so answer it first and record the answer.

=== SCOPE -- decide and implement ONE coherent rule, recording the reasoning ===

(1) Add the dispatching task's own resolved artifact directory as an implicit, unconditional in-scope member of site 2's containment predicate, mirroring sites 1 and 3.
(2) Decide WHERE that member belongs: in the shared definition (scripts/lib/engine-written-state-paths-lib.sh) so all three sites inherit one statement, or as a per-site splice as today. Weigh honestly: sites 1 and 3 both use per-site splices already, and the task directory is PER-TASK rather than a fixed literal path, so a shared literal allowlist may simply be the wrong home for it. State the ruling rather than defaulting to "share it because sharing is good."
(3) Record site 2's new member in git-staging-scope.md's "Three Containment sites, not one" section, with its relationship to sites 1 and 3 and to the staging seed, as project 425 did for site 1.

=== HARD CONSTRAINTS ===
- Do NOT weaken the containment predicate for a genuine excursion. Drop-and-warn for an out-of-territory source edit is correct and must survive intact, pinned by a test.
- Do NOT make the check fatal. Fail-open on a missing/empty/malformed file_scope, and never refusing a whole commit over this guard, are both deliberate and must stay. (This is separate from establishing WHY fail-open did not apply above -- diagnose that without removing the posture.)
- Do NOT re-introduce or disturb the trailing-slash glob normalization in `is_contained()` or the engine-written-paths allowlist; both are already present and working.
- Do NOT widen the staging seed to compensate; the seed is already correct. The defect is in the predicate.
- Any state.json write goes through the mutex-guarded state-write.sh path, never a second writer.

=== TERRITORY OVERLAP -- SEQUENCE, DO NOT PARALLELIZE ===
Open tasks 486 and 430 each declare agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/git-commit-phase.sh, scripts/tests/test-git-commit-phase.sh and context/standards/git-staging-scope.md in their own file_scope, and each changes the same containment predicate. This record is the narrowest of the three and is the natural predecessor; serializing dependency edges onto those two records were added at creation time -- tasks 486 and 430 each gained a dependency on this record, cycle-checked via validate-state.sh --deep. Neither subsumes this work: 486 concerns an extension's own manifest.json registration (not under any task directory), and 430 concerns stale hand-authored file_scope for SOURCE paths (its twenty cited drops are all agent-system/** files, none under a task's artifact tree). A task's own artifact directory is structurally engine territory that should never have required declaration at all, which is a different claim from either.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===
- A fixture proves a task whose declared, NON-EMPTY file_scope omits its own artifact directory has a report written under that directory land in its phase commit, with zero scope-excursion issue records emitted for it.
- A sibling fixture in the same run proves a genuinely out-of-territory source path is still dropped, still warned, and still recorded as a scope excursion.
- A fixture preserves the fail-open posture for a missing/empty/malformed file_scope.
- The answer to the `missing_key`-yet-dropped question above is recorded, with whatever follow-on it implies either fixed here or filed.
- git-staging-scope.md records site 2's member and its relationship to sites 1 and 3.

active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/formal/** (and agent-system/extensions/core/** if the chosen remedy reaches core) -- never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store (see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Resolve the extension's own source_dir from <project-root>/.claude-extensions.json and edit at the path mirroring the deployed one; note that file carries NO top-level source_dir, only per-extension entries, so resolve the `formal` entry specifically. REDEPLOY AFTERWARDS via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

ORIGIN: conclusion stage (channel b, agent-system changes) of an /orchestrate invocation over task 878 in ~/Projects/BimodalLogic, session sess_1793904111_6edc04. User-approved at the lead level.

SEVERITY: minor.

CITATION -- ~/Projects/BimodalLogic/specs/878_lplus_ztime_decidability_paper_proof_repair/issues.jsonl (that repository, NOT this one): iss_1793906824199_f2HBxS

LIVE SYMPTOM: validate-artifact.sh failed the report produced by that run's research dispatch (formal-research-agent, dispatch seq 1) -- missing the required `## Recommendations` section per report-format.md. It was patched by hand in a later phase. A research agent produced a report that its own format standard rejects, and nothing caught it at the point of authorship.

=== THE DIAGNOSIS ALREADY EXISTS AND WAS ONLY HALF-APPLIED -- READ IT FIRST ===

Abandoned project 166 ("Stop research reports drifting from validate-artifact.sh's required section headings") worked out this exact failure mode in full. Its findings, which this record inherits rather than re-deriving:

- THE SKELETON IS NOT ITSELF INVALID. validate-artifact.sh matches each required section with `grep -qE "^##+ ${section}"` -- an any-depth heading-prefix regex -- so a third-level `### Recommendations` DOES satisfy the check. The agent departed from its own template when writing a real report.
- CONTRIBUTING FACTOR (a), BURIAL: in the skeleton, `### Recommendations` is a third-level subsection of `## Findings`, while every other required section is top-level. An agent restructuring Findings for a real report gets no signal that this one subsection is load-bearing for validation.
- CONTRIBUTING FACTOR (b), NEAR-MISS TRAP: the same skeleton separately contains `## Context Extension Recommendations`. An agent writing that heading may reasonably believe the requirement is met. Project 166 recorded that the observed failing artifact contained exactly that heading.

Project 166's agent-side remedy LANDED IN CORE ONLY. agent-system/extensions/core/agents/general-research-agent.md now carries (around lines 386-395) a verbatim, explicitly non-paraphrasable statement of the five required headings, the `^##+ {section}` regex, the warning that the match is exact-text and not fuzzy, and both observed near-misses named outright (`## Recommended Next Steps` and `## Context Extension Recommendations`), with the instruction to keep the latter but never as a substitute. Project 166's own SCOPE line asked only for an enumeration of "every CORE agent carrying a report or summary skeleton," and its file_scope covered only core. The extension agents were never swept. Project 166 was then abandoned.

=== MEASURED THIS RUN (re-derive before editing) ===

All four of the formal extension's research agents -- agent-system/extensions/formal/agents/formal-research-agent.md, logic-research-agent.md, math-research-agent.md and physics-research-agent.md -- contain:
- exactly ONE occurrence each of the string "Recommendations": the buried `### Recommendations` nested under `## Findings` (formal-research-agent.md around line 188, alongside `### Cross-Domain Synthesis`);
- ZERO occurrences of "validate-artifact".

None of the four carries the verbatim-heading contract, the `^##+` matching rule, or either named near-miss. The exact shape project 166 diagnosed is intact in all four, and it has now failed in production. formal-research-agent.md names general-research-agent.md as its "Copy source" for the canonical report shape, but the warning block that copy source gained was never propagated.

=== SCOPE -- decide and implement ONE coherent rule, recording the reasoning ===

(1) Carry the verbatim required-heading contract into the formal extension's four research agents. Prefer a SINGLE referenceable statement the agents point at over a fourth and fifth verbatim copy: four divergent copies of one contract is the mechanism that produced this gap. If no suitable referenceable home exists, say so and state why a copy is the lesser evil.
(2) Decide whether to promote `### Recommendations` to a top-level `## Recommendations` in these four skeletons -- project 166's remedy (ii), which it explicitly permitted combining with the agent-side remedy. This removes contributing factor (a) STRUCTURALLY rather than relying on instruction-following, which is precisely what failed both times. Weigh the cost: it changes the report shape these agents emit, and `### Recommendations` currently sits deliberately inside the per-domain Findings structure.
(3) Decide whether an authorship-time check belongs here at all: whether these agents should run validate-artifact.sh against their own report before returning, or whether the gate belongs in the research postflight that already reaches the validator. Weigh a per-dispatch self-check's cost against a repair that currently happens by hand a phase later.
(4) Complete the sweep project 166 scoped but never ran outside core: machine-check EVERY extension agent carrying a report or summary skeleton against the validator's own REPORT_SECTIONS/SUMMARY_SECTIONS arrays using the validator's own regex -- not by eye -- and list any further gaps found. The typst and lean extensions' research agents are the obvious next candidates. Completed project 137 ("Give the lean research and implementation agents the artifact skeletons their general-* counterparts already have") did this shape of fix for the lean agents and is the model to follow for any gap this enumeration turns up; filing a separate record per extension is acceptable if the sweep is large.

=== HARD CONSTRAINTS ===
- Do NOT relax validate-artifact.sh's matching to make this green. Project 166 recorded this as dangerous and the ruling stands: a substring match would let `## Context Extension Recommendations` satisfy `Recommendations`, converting a true failure into a false pass. Do not weaken a check to make it pass.
- Keep `## Context Extension Recommendations` available as a distinct, useful section -- never as a substitute for the required heading.
- Pre-existing non-conforming artifacts authored before their agent gained a conforming contract are OUT OF SCOPE; they fail for a different reason and are a separate backfill question, as project 166 also recorded.
- If remedies (3) or (4) reach core scripts or other extensions' agents, widen file_scope at plan time; this record declares only the four formal agents.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===
- The exact failure is reproduced in a fixture (a report carrying `## Context Extension Recommendations` and/or `## Recommended Next Steps` but no `## Recommendations`), shown to fail before the remedy and pass after it.
- All four formal research agents' skeletons machine-check clean against the validator's own regex and its own required-section arrays.
- The enumeration required by scope item (4) is recorded, with any remaining gaps listed or filed.
- The ruling and its reasoning are recorded, including explicitly why the validator was NOT changed.

active_projects.title: Add per-repo storage and injection to the sapience extension
active_projects.description:
Give the sapience extension repo-scoped knowledge storage and per-dispatch context injection, so it can replace the memory extension's local vault substrate. This is the essential piece of the migration -- the other three tasks in this batch depend on it.

SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: `agent-system/extensions/sapience/**` and `agent-system/extensions/core/**`, never a deployed `.claude/**` tree, which is a gitignored disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store (see `rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md`). Resolve `source_dir` from `<project-root>/.claude-extensions.json` and edit at the path mirroring the deployed one. REDEPLOY AFTERWARDS via `deploy-headless.sh`.

== THE SCOPING MECHANISM IS ALREADY SETTLED, AND IT IS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE ==

Per-repo scoping works ONLY via a repo tag embedded in the KO's `provenance` string, filtered on read by `/v1/search`'s `source=` substring parameter. This was established empirically against the live host; do not re-derive it, and do not substitute the `project` field.

What was measured:
- A KO written with `provenance` containing `[repo:nvim]` is returned by `source=[repo:nvim]` and by `source=repo:nvim`, and is NOT returned by `source=[repo:bimodal]`. The filter acts as a hard pre-filter that dominates relevance ranking -- an unrelated query still returned only the repo-tagged row.
- The `project` field is a DEAD END. `/v1/search` silently ignores `&project=`: identical 8-row result sets for a real slug, another repo's slug, and a nonexistent slug. `/v1/sf1/handoff?project=X` merely echoes the slug back with `project_known: false` and returns cross-project KOs even for a bogus project. `/v1/sf1/state` returns 404. `/v1/projects` returns 403 `{"code": "company_only"}` -- project surfaces are a paid team feature on this account.
- `source_loc` (the field the `sapience_remember` MCP tool's own `source` argument populates) is NOT matched by the `source=` filter and is not returned in search results. A probe written with `source_loc: repo:/home/benjamin/.config/nvim` was not findable by that value; a probe with the tag in `provenance` was.
- CONSEQUENCE: the `sapience_remember` MCP tool CANNOT be used for tagged writes, because `mcp.py`'s `remember_provenance()` hardcodes provenance to `"<Name> via Claude Code session (MCP)"` with no injectable repo marker (an unknown `SAPIENCE_CLIENT` collapses to the label `AI`, so it cannot be smuggled in that way either). Tagged writes must go to `POST /ingest-kos` directly, which accepts an arbitrary `provenance` string verbatim.

== DELIVERABLE 1: sapience-retrieve.sh ==

A retrieval script calling `GET /v1/search?q=<keywords>&source=[repo:<slug>]&limit=5`, emitting the SAME `<memory-context>` envelope `memory-retrieve.sh` emits today, so the dispatch-side contract is unchanged. Preserve that script's existing budget discipline: 2000-token budget, 5-entry cap. Derive the repo slug from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (basename), so the same script works unmodified in every repo the system deploys into. Reuse `memory-retrieve.sh`'s existing keyword-extraction stage (lowercase, split on non-alpha, stop-word filter, length>3, top 10) rather than inventing a second one -- only the corpus lookup changes, not the query derivation.

Measured latency: 0.22s average over five cold queries against the live host, so per-dispatch injection is viable. The response's `meter` field is informational (`tokens_read`/`tokens_held`), not a search quota.

== DELIVERABLE 2: the dispatch swap ==

Swap the retrieval call in at `agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh`, at the existing memory-retrieval call site in its Stage 3.5 `memory_context` block (currently a `bash "${SKILL_REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/memory-retrieve.sh" "$description" "$task_type" "$memory_arg3" 2>/dev/null || memory_context=""` form, guarded by the `--clean` flag check).

PRESERVE THE FAILURE-SWALLOWING WRAPPER. The `2>/dev/null) || memory_context=""` shape means a failure degrades to no injection rather than a broken dispatch. This matters MORE after the swap than before it, because the new call is a network round-trip rather than a local jq pass -- an outage must not break every dispatch in a batch. Also preserve the `--clean` suppression semantics unchanged.

== DELIVERABLE 3: sapience-remember.sh ==

A write script calling `POST /ingest-kos` with the repo-tagged provenance AND `explicit: true`.

`explicit: true` IS MANDATORY, not an optimization. Measured: a realistically-worded probe note was silently discarded by the server's noise gate -- the response was `{"ok": true, "written": 0, "gated": 1}`, with `ok: true` despite nothing being written. The same note with `explicit: true` wrote successfully (`written: 1`). Without the flag, task findings would be lost invisibly, and the success-shaped response makes the loss undetectable from the caller side. The script MUST additionally treat `gated >= 1` as a loud, reported outcome rather than a silent success, so a future gate change cannot reintroduce silent loss.

== CONSTRAINTS AND KNOWN HAZARDS TO RECORD IN THE DESIGN ==

- THERE IS NO DELETE API. `DELETE /v1/ko/<hash>`, `DELETE /v1/kos/<hash>` and `POST /v1/ko/<hash>/delete` all return 404. Writes are permanent; deletion is web-app-only. This is the principal risk of any per-dispatch write path and MUST shape how much is written per task -- prefer few, high-value, well-formed writes at a task boundary over a write per decision.
- Writes through this path bypass the `auto_approve: false` review gate entirely (that gate governs only the transcript-extraction path), so every write is permanent and unreviewed. State this in the extension's own documentation.
- The transcript-extraction path CANNOT be repo-tagged, so it will keep writing untagged KOs that repo-filtered reads never see. The vault therefore accumulates two differently-shaped populations. Document this asymmetry rather than attempting to fix it.
- Two disposable probe KOs written during the research that established the above could not be deleted via API and need manual removal at app.spnc.ai: hashes `806180dc43c5cb34` ("sapience source_loc filter probe") and `9ba2b479b5e4a7e2` ("sapience provenance tagging probe"). Note this as a manual cleanup item; it is not implementation work.

== WHY THE DEPENDENCY EDGES EXIST ==

`orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh` is shared file territory with four non-terminal records (360, 449, 450, 487). Per the batching rule, shared territory means a declared edge and a serialized sequence, never a bare exclusion. 488 is declared because it owns `agent-system/extensions/sapience/settings-fragment.json` and `review-gate-boundary.md`, which this task's documentation deliverable touches.

== BACKLOG AUDIT DISPOSITION (adjudicated at the confirmation gate) ==

The audit's `duplicate-of-open #421` verdict is `mechanical_class: none` at 41% semantic similarity and was ruled NOT a duplicate: 421 concerns evidence consumption, not context injection. The `overlaps-open` verdicts against 360, 435, 449, 450 and 487 are real and are discharged by the declared dependency edges above.

== VERIFICATION ==

- A tagged write followed by a repo-filtered read returns that KO, and a read filtered to a DIFFERENT repo tag does not.
- A write whose response carries `gated >= 1` is reported as a failure by the script, not swallowed.
- With the retrieval endpoint unreachable (simulated), a dispatch still builds and runs with an empty `memory_context`, exactly as the current `|| memory_context=""` behaviour provides.
- `--clean` still suppresses injection after the swap.
- The emitted `<memory-context>` block is byte-comparable in shape to the one `memory-retrieve.sh` produces for an equivalent corpus, so no consumer needs changing.
